94.s:
brahmovāca
śvetatīrtham iti khyātaṃ trailokye viśrutaṃ śubham
tasya śravaṇamātreṇa sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
श्वेततीर्थम् इति ख्यातं त्रैलोक्ये विश्रुतं शुभम्
तस्य श्रवणमात्रेण सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
Renowned as Śvetatīrtha, auspicious, famous in the three worlds,
by the mere hearing of it one is freed from all sins.

94.s:
śveto nāma purā vipro gautamasya priyaḥ sakhā
ātithyapūjānirato gautamītīram āśritaḥ //
94.d:
श्वेतो नाम पुरा विप्रो गौतमस्य प्रियः सखा
आतिथ्यपूजानिरतो गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितः ॥
94.m:
Formerly, a twice-born named Śveta was a dear friend of Gautama,
devoted to hospitality and worship, settled on the bank of the Gautamī,

94.s:
manasā karmaṇā vācā śivabhaktiparāyaṇaḥ
dhyāyantaṃ taṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ pūjayantaṃ sadā śivam //
94.d:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा शिवभक्तिपरायणः
ध्यायन्तं तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं पूजयन्तं सदा शिवम् ॥
94.m:
dedicated to devotion to Śiva in mind, deed, and speech.
As that best of twice-born was meditating, always worshiping Śiva,

94.s:
pūrṇāyuṣaṃ dvijavaraṃ śivabhaktiparāyaṇam
netuṃ dūtāḥ samājagmur dakṣiṇāśāpates tadā //
94.d:
पूर्णायुषं द्विजवरं शिवभक्तिपरायणम्
नेतुं दूताः समाजग्मुर् दक्षिणाशापतेस् तदा ॥
94.m:
having completed his lifespan, the excellent twice-born dedicated to devotion to Śiva,
the messengers of the lord of the southern quarter then came to take him away.

94.s:
nāśaknuvan gṛhaṃ tasya praveṣṭum api nārada
tadā kāle vyatikrānte citrako mṛtyum abravīt //
94.d:
नाशक्नुवन् गृहं तस्य प्रवेष्टुम् अपि नारद
तदा काले व्यतिक्रान्ते चित्रको मृत्युम् अब्रवीत् ॥
94.m:
They were unable even to enter his house, O Nārada.
Then, as time elapsed, Citraka said to Mṛtyu:

94.s:
citraka uvāca
kiṃ nāyāti kṣīṇajīvo mṛtyo śvetaḥ kathaṃ tv iti
nādyāpy āyānti dūtās te mṛtyor naivocitaṃ tu te //
94.d:
चित्रक उवाच
किं नायाति क्षीणजीवो मृत्यो श्वेतः कथं त्व् इति
नाद्याप्य् आयान्ति दूतास् ते मृत्योर् नैवोचितं तु ते ॥
94.m:
Citraka said:
"Why does Śveta not arrive, his life having run out, O Mṛtyu? How is this?
Even now your messengers have not returned; indeed, this is not proper for you, [the god of] death."

94.s:
brahmovāca
tataś ca kupito mṛtyuḥ prāyāc chvetagṛhaṃ svayam
bahiḥsthitāṃs tadā paśyan mṛtyur dūtān bhayārditān
provāca kim idaṃ dūtā mṛtyum ūcuś ca dūtakāḥ //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततश् च कुपितो मृत्युः प्रायाच् छ्वेतगृहं स्वयम्
बहिःस्थितांस् तदा पश्यन् मृत्युर् दूतान् भयार्दितान्
प्रोवाच किम् इदं दूता मृत्युम् ऊचुश् च दूतकाः ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
Then, enraged, Mṛtyu went to Śveta's house himself.
Then, seeing the messengers standing outside, stricken with fear,
Mṛtyu spoke: "What is this, O messengers?" And the messengers said to Mṛtyu:

94.s:
dūtā ūcuḥ
śivena rakṣitaṃ śvetaṃ vayaṃ no vīkṣituṃ kṣamāḥ
yeṣāṃ prasanno giriśas teṣāṃ kā nāma bhītayaḥ //
94.d:
दूता ऊचुः
शिवेन रक्षितं श्वेतं वयं नो वीक्षितुं क्षमाः
येषां प्रसन्नो गिरिशस् तेषां का नाम भीतयः ॥
94.m:
The messengers said:
"We are not able to look upon Śveta, who is protected by Śiva.
For those with whom the mountain-dweller is pleased, what fears indeed can there be?"

94.s:
brahmovāca
pāśapāṇis tadā mṛtyuḥ prāviśad yatra sa dvijaḥ
nāsau vipro vijānāti mṛtyuṃ vā yamakiṃkarān //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पाशपाणिस् तदा मृत्युः प्राविशद् यत्र स द्विजः
नासौ विप्रो विजानाति मृत्युं वा यमकिंकरान् ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
Then Mṛtyu, with noose in hand, entered where the twice-born was.
That twice-born did not notice Mṛtyu or the servants of Yama.

94.s:
śivaṃ pūjayate bhaktyā śvetasya tu samīpataḥ
mṛtyuṃ pāśadharaṃ dṛṣṭvā daṇḍī provāca vismitaḥ //
94.d:
शिवं पूजयते भक्त्या श्वेतस्य तु समीपतः
मृत्युं पाशधरं दृष्ट्वा दण्डी प्रोवाच विस्मितः ॥
94.m:
He was worshiping Śiva with devotion. But near Śveta,
seeing Mṛtyu holding a noose, Daṇḍin said in amazement:

94.s:
daṇḍy uvāca
kim atra vīkṣase mṛtyo daṇḍinaṃ mṛtyur abravīt //
94.d:
दण्ड्य् उवाच
किम् अत्र वीक्षसे मृत्यो दण्डिनं मृत्युर् अब्रवीत् ॥
94.m:
Daṇḍin said:
"What do you behold here, O Mṛtyu?" Mṛtyu said to Daṇḍin:

94.s:
mṛtyur uvāca
śvetaṃ netum ihāyātas tasmād vīkṣe dvijottamam //
94.d:
मृत्युर् उवाच
श्वेतं नेतुम् इहायातस् तस्माद् वीक्षे द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
94.m:
Mṛtyu said:
"I have come here to take Śveta; therefore I look upon the best of the twice-born."

94.s:
brahmovāca
tvaṃ gacchety abravīd daṇḍī mṛtyuḥ pāśān athākṣipat
śvetāya muniśārdūla tato daṇḍī cukopa ha //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
त्वं गच्छेत्य् अब्रवीद् दण्डी मृत्युः पाशान् अथाक्षिपत्
श्वेताय मुनिशार्दूल ततो दण्डी चुकोप ह ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
"Go away!" Daṇḍin said. Then Mṛtyu hurled his nooses
at Śveta, O tiger among sages; thereupon Daṇḍin became enraged.

94.s:
śivadattena daṇḍena daṇḍī mṛtyum atāḍayat
tataḥ pāśadharo mṛtyuḥ papāta dharaṇītale //
94.d:
शिवदत्तेन दण्डेन दण्डी मृत्युम् अताडयत्
ततः पाशधरो मृत्युः पपात धरणीतले ॥
94.m:
With the staff given by Śiva, Daṇḍin struck Mṛtyu;
then Mṛtyu, holding his noose, fell onto the surface of the earth.

94.s:
tatas te satvaraṃ dūtā hataṃ mṛtyum avekṣya ca
yamāya sarvam avadan vadhaṃ mṛtyos tu daṇḍinā //
94.d:
ततस् ते सत्वरं दूता हतं मृत्युम् अवेक्ष्य च
यमाय सर्वम् अवदन् वधं मृत्योस् तु दण्डिना ॥
94.m:
Then those messengers, seeing Mṛtyu slain, quickly
told Yama everything about the slaying of Mṛtyu by Daṇḍin.

94.s:
tataś ca kupito dharmo yamo mahiṣavāhanaḥ
citraguptaṃ bahubalaṃ yamadaṇḍaṃ ca rakṣakam //
94.d:
ततश् च कुपितो धर्मो यमो महिषवाहनः
चित्रगुप्तं बहुबलं यमदण्डं च रक्षकम् ॥
94.m:
Then Dharma, Yama, whose mount is a buffalo, became enraged,
[summoning] Citragupta of great might, and Yamadaṇḍa the guardian,

94.s:
mahiṣaṃ bhūtavetālān ādhivyādhīṃs tathaiva ca
akṣirogān kukṣirogān karṇaśūlaṃ tathaiva ca //
94.d:
महिषं भूतवेतालान् आधिव्याधींस् तथैव च
अक्षिरोगान् कुक्षिरोगान् कर्णशूलं तथैव च ॥
94.m:
the buffalo, the bhūtas, vetālas, mental ailments and physical diseases,
eye diseases, belly diseases, earache,

94.s:
jvaraṃ ca trividhaṃ pāpaṃ narakāṇi pṛthak pṛthak
tvarantām iti tān uktvā jagāma tvarito yamaḥ //
94.d:
ज्वरं च त्रिविधं पापं नरकाणि पृथक् पृथक्
त्वरन्ताम् इति तान् उक्त्वा जगाम त्वरितो यमः ॥
94.m:
fever, threefold sin, and the various hells separately.
Saying to them, "Hurry!", Yama departed in haste,

94.s:
etair anyaiḥ parivṛto yatra śveto dvijottamaḥ
tam āyāntaṃ yamaṃ dṛṣṭvā nandī provāca sāyudhaḥ //
94.d:
एतैर् अन्यैः परिवृतो यत्र श्वेतो द्विजोत्तमः
तम् आयान्तं यमं दृष्ट्वा नन्दी प्रोवाच सायुधः ॥
94.m:
surrounded by these and others, to where the twice-born Śveta was.
Seeing that Yama approaching, Nandī, armed with weapons, spoke

94.s:
vināyakaṃ tathā skandaṃ bhūtanāthaṃ tu daṇḍinam
tatra tad yuddham abhavat sarvalokabhayāvaham //
94.d:
विनायकं तथा स्कन्दं भूतनाथं तु दण्डिनम्
तत्र तद् युद्धम् अभवत् सर्वलोकभयावहम् ॥
94.m:
to Vināyaka, and Skanda, and the lord of bhūtas, Daṇḍin.
There a battle took place, terrifying to all the worlds.

94.s:
kārttikeyaḥ svayaṃ śaktyā bibheda yamakiṃkarān
dakṣiṇāśāpatiṃ cāpi nijaghāna balānvitam //
94.d:
कार्त्तिकेयः स्वयं शक्त्या बिभेद यमकिंकरान्
दक्षिणाशापतिं चापि निजघान बलान्वितम् ॥
94.m:
Kārttikeya himself pierced Yama's servants with his spear,
and he also struck down the mighty lord of the southern quarter.

94.s:
hatāvaśiṣṭā yāmyās te ādityāya nyavedayan
ādityo 'pi suraiḥ sārdhaṃ śrutvā tan mahad adbhutam //
94.d:
हतावशिष्टा याम्यास् ते आदित्याय न्यवेदयन्
आदित्यो ऽपि सुरैः सार्धं श्रुत्वा तन् महद् अद्भुतम् ॥
94.m:
Those servants of Yama who remained from the slaughter reported to Āditya.
Āditya too, hearing of that great wonder, along with the gods

94.s:
lokapālair anuvṛto mamāntikam upāgamat
ahaṃ viṣṇuś ca bhagavān indro 'gnir varuṇas tathā //
94.d:
लोकपालैर् अनुवृतो ममान्तिकम् उपागमत्
अहं विष्णुश् च भगवान् इन्द्रो ऽग्निर् वरुणस् तथा ॥
94.m:
and accompanied by the world-guardians, came near me.
I, the lord Viṣṇu, Indra, Agni, and Varuṇa,

94.s:
candrādityāv aśvinau ca lokapālā marudgaṇāḥ
ete cānye ca bahavo vayaṃ yātā yamāntikam //
94.d:
चन्द्रादित्याव् अश्विनौ च लोकपाला मरुद्गणाः
एते चान्ये च बहवो वयं याता यमान्तिकम् ॥
94.m:
Candra and Āditya, the Aśvins, the world-guardians, the hosts of Maruts,
these and many others, we went to Yama's presence.

94.s:
mṛta āste dakṣiṇeśo gaṅgātīre balānvitaḥ
samudrāś ca nadā nāgā nānābhūtāny anekaśaḥ //
94.d:
मृत आस्ते दक्षिणेशो गङ्गातीरे बलान्वितः
समुद्राश् च नदा नागा नानाभूतान्य् अनेकशः ॥
94.m:
The mighty lord of the south lay dead on the bank of the Gaṅgā.
The oceans, rivers, nāgas, and various beings in great numbers

94.s:
tatrājagmuḥ sureśānaṃ draṣṭuṃ vaivasvataṃ yamam
taṃ dṛṣṭvā hatasainyaṃ ca yamaṃ devā bhayārditāḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ śaṃbhum ūcuḥ sarve punaḥ punaḥ //
94.d:
तत्राजग्मुः सुरेशानं द्रष्टुं वैवस्वतं यमम्
तं दृष्ट्वा हतसैन्यं च यमं देवा भयार्दिताः
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः शंभुम् ऊचुः सर्वे पुनः पुनः ॥
94.m:
came there to see the lord of the gods, Yama the son of Vivasvat.
Seeing him and his army slain, the gods, distressed with fear,
with folded hands, spoke to Śambhu again and again:

94.s:
devā ūcuḥ
bhaktipriyatvaṃ te nityaṃ duṣṭahantṛtvam eva ca
ādikartar namas tubhyaṃ nīlakaṇṭha namo 'stu te
brahmapriya namas te 'stu devapriya namo 'stu te //
94.d:
देवा ऊचुः
भक्तिप्रियत्वं ते नित्यं दुष्टहन्तृत्वम् एव च
आदिकर्तर् नमस् तुभ्यं नीलकण्ठ नमो ऽस्तु ते
ब्रह्मप्रिय नमस् ते ऽस्तु देवप्रिय नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
94.m:
The gods said:
"Devotion is ever dear to you, and you are the destroyer of the wicked.
Homage to you, original creator! O blue-throated one, homage be to you!
O beloved of Brahmā, homage be to you! O beloved of the gods, homage be to you!

94.s:
śvetaṃ dvijaṃ bhaktam anāyuṣaṃ te
netuṃ yamādiḥ sakalo 'samarthaḥ
saṃtoṣam āptāḥ paramaṃ samīkṣya
bhaktapriyatvaṃ tvayi nātha satyam
94.d:
श्वेतं द्विजं भक्तम् अनायुषं ते
नेतुं यमादिः सकलो ऽसमर्थः
संतोषम् आप्ताः परमं समीक्ष्य
भक्तप्रियत्वं त्वयि नाथ सत्यम्
94.m: To take the twice-born Śveta, your devotee, whose lifespan was ended, / Yama and the rest were entirely unable. / Having seen this, we have attained supreme satisfaction; / love for your devotees is truly in you, O Lord!

94.s:
ye tvāṃ prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ kṛpāluṃ
nālaṃ kṛtānto 'py anuvīkṣituṃ tān
evaṃ viditvā śiva eva sarve
tvām eva bhaktyā parayā bhajante
94.d:
ये त्वां प्रपन्नाः शरणं कृपालुं
नालं कृतान्तो ऽप्य् अनुवीक्षितुं तान्
एवं विदित्वा शिव एव सर्वे
त्वाम् एव भक्त्या परया भजन्ते
94.m: For those who have sought refuge in you, the compassionate one, / even the Ender is not able to look upon them. / Knowing this, everyone with supreme devotion / worships you alone, O Śiva!

94.s:
tvam eva jagatāṃ nātha kiṃ na smarasi śaṃkara
tvāṃ vinā kaḥ samartho 'tra vyavasthāṃ kartum īśvaraḥ //
94.d:
त्वम् एव जगतां नाथ किं न स्मरसि शंकर
त्वां विना कः समर्थो ऽत्र व्यवस्थां कर्तुम् ईश्वरः ॥
94.m:
You alone are the master of the worlds; do you not remember, O Śaṅkara?
Without you, what lord is able to establish cosmic order here?"

94.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ tu stuvatāṃ teṣāṃ purastād abhavac chivaḥ
kiṃ dadāmīti tān āha idam ūcuḥ surā api //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं तु स्तुवतां तेषां पुरस्ताद् अभवच् छिवः
किं ददामीति तान् आह इदम् ऊचुः सुरा अपि ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
As they were thus praising him, Śiva appeared before them.
He said to them, "What shall I grant?" And the gods also spoke this:

94.s:
devā ūcuḥ
ayaṃ vaivasvato dharmo niyantā sarvadehinām
dharmādharmavyavasthāyāṃ sthāpito lokapālakaḥ //
94.d:
देवा ऊचुः
अयं वैवस्वतो धर्मो नियन्ता सर्वदेहिनाम्
धर्माधर्मव्यवस्थायां स्थापितो लोकपालकः ॥
94.m:
The gods said:
"This Dharma, the son of Vivasvat, is the controller of all embodied beings,
established as a world-guardian in the order of dharma and adharma.

94.s:
nāyaṃ vadham avāpnoti nāparādhī na pāpakṛt
vinā tena jagaddhātur naiva kiṃcid bhaviṣyati //
94.d:
नायं वधम् अवाप्नोति नापराधी न पापकृत्
विना तेन जगद्धातुर् नैव किंचिद् भविष्यति ॥
94.m:
He does not deserve slaughter; he is not an offender, nor an evildoer.
Without him, nothing of the creator of the world can proceed.

94.s:
tasmāj jīvaya deveśa yamaṃ sabalavāhanam
prārthanā saphalā nātha mahatsu na vṛthā bhavet //
94.d:
तस्माज् जीवय देवेश यमं सबलवाहनम्
प्रार्थना सफला नाथ महत्सु न वृथा भवेत् ॥
94.m:
Therefore revive Yama, along with his army and mount, O lord of the gods!
May a request, O Lord, bear fruit and not be in vain among the great."

94.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ provāca bhagavāñ jīvayeyam asaṃśayam
yamaṃ yadi vaco me 'dya anumanyanti devatāḥ //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्रोवाच भगवाञ् जीवयेयम् असंशयम्
यमं यदि वचो मे ऽद्य अनुमन्यन्ति देवताः ॥
94.m:
Brahmā said:
Then the Lord said, "I shall revive Yama without doubt,
if the gods today assent to my word."

94.s:
tataḥ procuḥ surāḥ sarve kurmo vākyaṃ tvayoditam
haribrahmādisahitaṃ vaśe yasyākhilaṃ jagat //
94.d:
ततः प्रोचुः सुराः सर्वे कुर्मो वाक्यं त्वयोदितम्
हरिब्रह्मादिसहितं वशे यस्याखिलं जगत् ॥
94.m:
Then all the gods said, "We will perform the word spoken by you,
under whose control is the entire world, together with Hari, Brahmā, and the others."

94.s:
tataḥ provāca bhagavān amarān samupāgatān
madbhakto na mṛtiṃ yātu nety ūcur amarāḥ punaḥ //
94.d:
ततः प्रोवाच भगवान् अमरान् समुपागतान्
मद्भक्तो न मृतिं यातु नेत्य् ऊचुर् अमराः पुनः ॥
94.m:
Then the Lord said to the gods who had assembled:
"Let my devotee not go to death." The immortals said again, "No [he will not]."

94.s:
amarāḥ syus tato deva sarvalokāś carācarāḥ
amartyamartyabhedo 'yaṃ na syād deva jaganmaya //
94.d:
अमराः स्युस् ततो देव सर्वलोकाश् चराचराः
अमर्त्यमर्त्यभेदो ऽयं न स्याद् देव जगन्मय ॥
94.m: “All the worlds of moving and unmoving beings would then become immortal, O Lord! / This distinction between immortal and mortal would no longer exist, O God who pervades the universe!”

94.s:
punar apy āha tāñ śaṃbhuḥ śṛṇvantu mama bhāṣitam
madbhaktānāṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ gautamīm anusevatām //
94.d:
पुनर् अप्य् आह ताञ् शंभुः शृण्वन्तु मम भाषितम्
मद्भक्तानां वैष्णवानां गौतमीम् अनुसेवताम् ॥
94.m: Śambhu spoke again to them: “Listen to what I say. / For my devotees, for the Vaiṣṇavas, and for those who serve the Gautamī,

94.s:
vayaṃ tu svāmino nityaṃ na mṛtyuḥ svāmyam arhati
vārttāpy eṣāṃ na kartavyā yamena tu kadācana //
94.d:
वयं तु स्वामिनो नित्यं न मृत्युः स्वाम्यम् अर्हति
वार्त्ताप्य् एषां न कर्तव्या यमेन तु कदाचन ॥
94.m: we are always the masters; Death has no right of ownership. / Not even a mention of them is ever to be made by Yama.

94.s:
ādhivyādhyādibhir jātu kāryo nābhibhavaḥ kvacit
ye śivaṃ śaraṇaṃ yātās te muktās tatkṣaṇād api //
94.d:
आधिव्याध्यादिभिर् जातु कार्यो नाभिभवः क्वचित्
ये शिवं शरणं यातास् ते मुक्तास् तत्क्षणाद् अपि ॥
94.m: Mental afflictions, physical illnesses, and the like should never overcome them anywhere. / Those who take refuge in Śiva are liberated that very moment.

94.s:
sānugasya yamasyāto namasyāḥ sarva eva te
tathety ūcuḥ suragaṇā devadevaṃ śivaṃ prati //
94.d:
सानुगस्य यमस्यातो नमस्याः सर्व एव ते
तथेत्य् ऊचुः सुरगणा देवदेवं शिवं प्रति ॥
94.m: Therefore, all of them are to be bowed down to by Yama and his attendants.” / “So be it,” said the hosts of gods to Śiva, the god of gods.

94.s: tataś ca bhagavān nātho nandinaṃ prāha vāhanam //
94.d: ततश् च भगवान् नाथो नन्दिनं प्राह वाहनम् ॥
94.m: And then the blessed Lord spoke to his mount, Nandin.

94.s:
śiva uvāca
gautamyā udakena tvam abhiṣiñca mṛtaṃ yamam //
94.d:
शिव उवाच
गौतम्या उदकेन त्वम् अभिषिञ्च मृतं यमम् ॥
94.m: Śiva said: / “Sprinkle the dead Yama with the water of the Gautamī.”

94.s:
brahmovāca
tato yamādayaḥ sarve abhiṣiktās tu nandinā
utthitāś ca sajīvās te dakṣiṇāśāṃ tato gatāḥ //
94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो यमादयः सर्वे अभिषिक्तास् तु नन्दिना
उत्थिताश् च सजीवास् ते दक्षिणाशां ततो गताः ॥
94.m: Brahmā said: / Then all of them, Yama and the others, sprinkled by Nandin, / arose alive, and then departed to the southern quarter.

94.s:
uttare gautamītīre viṣṇvādyāḥ sarvadaivatāḥ
sthitā āsan pūjayanto devadevaṃ maheśvaram //
94.d:
उत्तरे गौतमीतीरे विष्ण्वाद्याः सर्वदैवताः
स्थिता आसन् पूजयन्तो देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ॥
94.m: On the northern bank of the Gautamī, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu / remained, worshipping the god of gods, Maheśvara.

94.s:
tatrāsann ayutāny aṣṭa sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
tathā ṣaṭ ca sahasrāṇi punaḥ ṣaṭ ca tathaiva ca //
94.d:
तत्रासन्न् अयुतान्य् अष्ट सहस्राणि चतुर्दश
तथा षट् च सहस्राणि पुनः षट् च तथैव च ॥
94.m: There were eighty thousand, fourteen thousand, / and six thousand, and again six likewise,

94.s:
ṣaḍ dakṣiṇe tathā tīre tīrthānām ayutatrayam
puṇyam ākhyānam etad dhi śvetatīrthasya nārada //
94.d:
षड् दक्षिणे तथा तीरे तीर्थानाम् अयुतत्रयम्
पुण्यम् आख्यानम् एतद् धि श्वेततीर्थस्य नारद ॥
94.m: and six, and on the southern bank thirty thousand tīrthas. / This is the holy narrative of the Śvetatīrtha, O Nārada.

94.s:
yatrāsau patito mṛtyur mṛtyutīrthaṃ tad ucyate
tasya śravaṇamātreṇa sahasraṃ jīvate samāḥ //
94.d:
यत्रासौ पतितो मृत्युर् मृत्युतीर्थं तद् उच्यते
तस्य श्रवणमात्रेण सहस्रं जीवते समाः ॥
94.m: Where that Death fell is called Mṛtyutīrtha; / merely by hearing of it, one lives for a thousand years.

94.s:
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
śravaṇaṃ paṭhanaṃ cāpi smaraṇaṃ ca malakṣayam
karoti sarvalokānāṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakam //
94.d:
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्
श्रवणं पठनं चापि स्मरणं च मलक्षयम्
करोति सर्वलोकानां भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम् ॥
94.m: Bathing and giving gifts there destroys all sins; / hearing, reciting, and even remembering it causes the destruction of impurity, / conferring enjoyment and liberation upon all people.

95.s:
brahmovāca
śukratīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvasiddhikaraṃ nṛṇām
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvavyādhivināśanam //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शुक्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिकरं नृणाम्
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / Known as Śukratīrtha, it grants all accomplishments to men; / it pacifies all sins and destroys all diseases.

95.s:
aṅgirāś ca bhṛguś caiva ṛṣī paramadhārmikau
tayoḥ putrau mahāprājñau rūpabuddhivilāsinau //
95.d:
अङ्गिराश् च भृगुश् चैव ऋषी परमधार्मिकौ
तयोः पुत्रौ महाप्राज्ञौ रूपबुद्धिविलासिनौ ॥
95.m: Aṅgiras and Bhṛgu were both most righteous sages. / Their two sons were very wise, graceful with beauty and intellect,

95.s:
jīvaḥ kavir iti khyātau mātāpitror vaśe ratau
upanītau sutau dṛṣṭvā pitarāv ūcatur mithaḥ //
95.d:
जीवः कविर् इति ख्यातौ मातापित्रोर् वशे रतौ
उपनीतौ सुतौ दृष्ट्वा पितराव् ऊचतुर् मिथः ॥
95.m: known as Jīva and Kavi, devoted to submission to their parents. / Seeing their two sons invested with the sacred thread, the two fathers spoke to each other.

95.s:
ṛṣī ūcatuḥ
āvayor eka evāstu śāstā nityaṃ ca putrayoḥ
tasmād ekaḥ śāsitā syāt tiṣṭhatv eko yathāsukham //
95.d:
ऋषी ऊचतुः
आवयोर् एक एवास्तु शास्ता नित्यं च पुत्रयोः
तस्माद् एकः शासिता स्यात् तिष्ठत्व् एको यथासुखम् ॥
95.m: The two sages said: / “Let only one of us be the constant instructor of our two sons. / Therefore let one be the teacher; let the other remain at his ease.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā tataḥ śīghram aṅgirāḥ prāha bhārgavam
adhyāpayiṣye sadṛśaṃ sukhaṃ tiṣṭhatu bhārgavaḥ //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा ततः शीघ्रम् अङ्गिराः प्राह भार्गवम्
अध्यापयिष्ये सदृशं सुखं तिष्ठतु भार्गवः ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this, Aṅgiras then quickly said to Bhārgava: / “I will teach them equally; let Bhārgava remain at ease.”

95.s:
etac chrutvā cāṅgiraso vākyaṃ bhṛgukulodvahaḥ
tatheti matvāṅgirase śukraṃ tasmai nyavedayat //
95.d:
एतच् छ्रुत्वा चाङ्गिरसो वाक्यं भृगुकुलोद्वहः
तथेति मत्वाङ्गिरसे शुक्रं तस्मै न्यवेदयत् ॥
95.m: Hearing these words of Aṅgiras, the descendant of Bhṛgu's lineage, / thinking, “So be it,” entrusted Śukra to Aṅgiras.

95.s:
ubhāv api sutau nityam adhyāpayati vai pṛthak
vaiṣamyabuddhyā tau bālau cirāc chukro 'bravīd idam //
95.d:
उभाव् अपि सुतौ नित्यम् अध्यापयति वै पृथक्
वैषम्यबुद्ध्या तौ बालौ चिराच् छुक्रो ऽब्रवीद् इदम् ॥
95.m: He constantly taught both boys separately, / with an attitude of partiality. After a long time, Śukra said this:

95.s:
śukra uvāca
vaiṣamyeṇa guro māṃ tvam adhyāpayasi nityaśaḥ
gurūṇāṃ nedam ucitaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ putraśiṣyayoḥ //
95.d:
शुक्र उवाच
वैषम्येण गुरो मां त्वम् अध्यापयसि नित्यशः
गुरूणां नेदम् उचितं वैषम्यं पुत्रशिष्ययोः ॥
95.m: Śukra said: / “O Guru, you constantly teach me with partiality. / Such partiality between a son and a disciple is not fitting for teachers.

95.s:
vaiṣamyeṇa ca vartante mūḍhāḥ śiṣyeṣu deśikāḥ
naiṣā viṣamabuddhīnāṃ saṃkhyā pāpasya vidyate //
95.d:
वैषम्येण च वर्तन्ते मूढाः शिष्येषु देशिकाः
नैषा विषमबुद्धीनां संख्या पापस्य विद्यते ॥
95.m: Foolish preceptors act with partiality toward disciples; / of those with partial minds, there is no counting of the sin.

95.s:
ācārya samyag jñāto 'si namasye 'haṃ punaḥ punaḥ
gaccheyaṃ gurum anyaṃ vai mām anujñātum arhasi //
95.d:
आचार्य सम्यग् ज्ञातो ऽसि नमस्ये ऽहं पुनः पुनः
गच्छेयं गुरुम् अन्यं वै माम् अनुज्ञातुम् अर्हसि ॥
95.m: O Master, you have been fully understood; I bow to you again and again. / I would go to another teacher; please grant me permission.

95.s:
gaccheyaṃ pitaraṃ brahman yady asau viṣamo bhavet
tato vānyatra gacchāmi svāmin pṛṣṭo 'si gamyate //
95.d:
गच्छेयं पितरं ब्रह्मन् यद्य् असौ विषमो भवेत्
ततो वान्यत्र गच्छामि स्वामिन् पृष्टो ऽसि गम्यते ॥
95.m: I might go to my father, O brahmin; if he should be partial, / then I will go elsewhere. O master, having asked you, I depart.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
guruṃ bṛhaspatiṃ dṛṣṭvā anujñātas tv agāt tataḥ
avāptavidyaḥ pitaraṃ gaccheyaṃ cety acintayat //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गुरुं बृहस्पतिं दृष्ट्वा अनुज्ञातस् त्व् अगात् ततः
अवाप्तविद्यः पितरं गच्छेयं चेत्य् अचिन्तयत् ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / Seeing the guru Bṛhaspati, and permitted [to leave], he departed from there. / “Having acquired knowledge, I should go to my father,” he thought.

95.s:
tasmāt kam anupṛccheyam utkṛṣṭaḥ ko gurur bhavet
iti smaran mahāprājñam apṛcchad vṛddhagautamam //
95.d:
तस्मात् कम् अनुपृच्छेयम् उत्कृष्टः को गुरुर् भवेत्
इति स्मरन् महाप्राज्ञम् अपृच्छद् वृद्धगौतमम् ॥
95.m: “Therefore, whom should I ask? Who would be a superior guru?” / Reflecting thus, he asked the venerable elder Gautama.

95.s:
śukra uvāca
ko guruḥ syān muniśreṣṭha mama brūhi gurur bhavet
trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yo gurus taṃ vrajāmy aham //
95.d:
शुक्र उवाच
को गुरुः स्यान् मुनिश्रेष्ठ मम ब्रूहि गुरुर् भवेत्
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानां यो गुरुस् तं व्रजाम्य् अहम् ॥
95.m: Śukra said: / “Who can be a guru, O best of sages? Tell me who could be my guru. / I shall go to him who is the guru of even the three worlds.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
sa prāha jagatām īśaṃ śaṃbhuṃ devaṃ jagadgurum
kvārādhayāmi giriśam ity uktaḥ prāha gautamaḥ //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स प्राह जगताम् ईशं शंभुं देवं जगद्गुरुम्
क्वाराधयामि गिरिशम् इत्य् उक्तः प्राह गौतमः ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / He named Śambhu, the Lord of the worlds, the god who is the guru of the universe. / When asked, “Where may I worship the mountain-dwelling Lord?”, Gautama replied:

95.s:
gautama uvāca
gautamyāṃ tu śucir bhūtvā stotrais toṣaya śaṃkaram
tatas tuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ sa te vidyāṃ pradāsyati //
95.d:
गौतम उवाच
गौतम्यां तु शुचिर् भूत्वा स्तोत्रैस् तोषय शंकरम्
ततस् तुष्टो जगन्नाथः स ते विद्यां प्रदास्यति ॥
95.m: Gautama said: / “Having become pure at the Gautamī, please Śaṅkara with hymns of praise. / Then, being pleased, the Lord of the Universe will grant you knowledge.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
gautamasya tu tadvākyāt prāgād gaṅgāṃ sa bhārgavaḥ
snātvā bhūtvā śuciḥ samyak stutiṃ cakre sa bālakaḥ //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गौतमस्य तु तद्वाक्यात् प्रागाद् गङ्गां स भार्गवः
स्नात्वा भूत्वा शुचिः सम्यक् स्तुतिं चक्रे स बालकः ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / By those words of Gautama, that descendant of Bhṛgu went to the Gaṅgā. / Having bathed and become thoroughly pure, the boy offered praise.

95.s:
śukra uvāca
bālo 'haṃ bālabuddhiś ca bālacandradhara prabho
nāhaṃ jānāmi te kiṃcit stutiṃ kartuṃ namo 'stu te //
95.d:
शुक्र उवाच
बालो ऽहं बालबुद्धिश् च बालचन्द्रधर प्रभो
नाहं जानामि ते किंचित् स्तुतिं कर्तुं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
95.m: Śukra said: / “I am a boy and child-minded, O Lord who bears the crescent moon! / I do not know how to compose any praise of you; obeisance be to you!

95.s:
parityaktasya guruṇā na mamāsti suhṛt sakhā
tvaṃ prabhuḥ sarvabhāvena jagannātha namo 'stu te //
95.d:
परित्यक्तस्य गुरुणा न ममास्ति सुहृत् सखा
त्वं प्रभुः सर्वभावेन जगन्नाथ नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
95.m: Abandoned by my guru, I have neither friend nor companion. / You are the Lord in every respect, O Lord of the Universe! Obeisance be to you!

95.s:
gurur gurumatāṃ deva mahatāṃ ca mahān asi
aham alpataro bālo jaganmaya namo 'stu te //
95.d:
गुरुर् गुरुमतां देव महतां च महान् असि
अहम् अल्पतरो बालो जगन्मय नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
95.m: You are the guru of those who possess gurus, O God, and great among the great. / I am a tiny boy, O you who pervade the universe! Obeisance be to you!

95.s:
vidyārthaṃ hi sureśāna nāhaṃ vedmi bhavadgatim
māṃ tvaṃ ca kṛpayā paśya lokasākṣin namo 'stu te //
95.d:
विद्यार्थं हि सुरेशान नाहं वेद्मि भवद्गतिम्
मां त्वं च कृपया पश्य लोकसाक्षिन् नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
95.m: For the sake of knowledge, O Lord of the gods, though I do not understand your course, / look upon me with compassion, O witness of the world! Obeisance be to you!”

95.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ tu stuvatas tasya prasanno 'bhūt sureśvaraḥ //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं तु स्तुवतस् तस्य प्रसन्नो ऽभूत् सुरेश्वरः ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / As he was praising him thus, the Lord of the gods became pleased.

95.s:
śiva uvāca
kāmaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yac cāpi suradurlabham //
95.d:
शिव उवाच
कामं वरय भद्रं ते यच् चापि सुरदुर्लभम् ॥
95.m: Śiva said: / “Choose a boon as you wish, bless you, even that which is difficult for gods to attain.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
kavir apy āha deveśaṃ kṛtāñjalir udāradhīḥ //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कविर् अप्य् आह देवेशं कृताञ्जलिर् उदारधीः ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / Kavi too, noble-minded, with folded hands said to the Lord of the gods:

95.s:
śukra uvāca
brahmādibhiś ca ṛṣibhir yā vidyā naiva gocarā
tāṃ vidyāṃ nātha yāciṣye tvaṃ gurur mama daivatam //
95.d:
शुक्र उवाच
ब्रह्मादिभिश् च ऋषिभिर् या विद्या नैव गोचरा
तां विद्यां नाथ याचिष्ये त्वं गुरुर् मम दैवतम् ॥
95.m: Śukra said: / “The knowledge that is beyond the scope even of Brahmā and other sages— / that knowledge I shall ask for, O Lord; you are my guru, my divinity.”

95.s:
brahmovāca
mṛtasaṃjīvinīṃ vidyām ajñātāṃ tridaśair api
tāṃ dattavān suraśreṣṭhas tasmai śukrāya yācate //
95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मृतसंजीविनीं विद्याम् अज्ञातां त्रिदशैर् अपि
तां दत्तवान् सुरश्रेष्ठस् तस्मै शुक्राय याचते ॥
95.m: Brahmā said: / The lore that brings the dead back to life, unknown even to the thirty [gods]— / that the best of gods gave to Śukra who asked for it.

95.s:
itarā laukikī vidyā vaidikī cānyagocarā
kiṃ punaḥ śaṃkare tuṣṭe vicāryam avaśiṣyate //
95.d:
इतरा लौकिकी विद्या वैदिकी चान्यगोचरा
किं पुनः शंकरे तुष्टे विचार्यम् अवशिष्यते ॥
95.m: Other knowledge is worldly, and Vedic [lore] is within the reach of others; / what further deliberation remains once Śaṅkara is pleased?

95.s:
sa tu labdhvā mahāvidyāṃ prāyāt svapitaraṃ gurum
daityānāṃ ca guruś cāsīd vidyayā pūjitaḥ kaviḥ //
95.d:
स तु लब्ध्वा महाविद्यां प्रायात् स्वपितरं गुरुम्
दैत्यानां च गुरुश् चासीद् विद्यया पूजितः कविः ॥
95.m: Having obtained the great lore, he went to his own father, his teacher; / and Kavi, honoured for his knowledge, became the guru of the Daityas.

95.s:
tataḥ kadācit tāṃ vidyāṃ kasmiṃścit kāraṇāntare
kaco bṛhaspatisuto vidyāṃ prāptaḥ kaves tu tām //
95.d:
ततः कदाचित् तां विद्यां कस्मिंश्चित् कारणान्तरे
कचो बृहस्पतिसुतो विद्यां प्राप्तः कवेस् तु ताम् ॥
95.m: Then, once, on a certain occasion, / Kaca, the son of Bṛhaspati, obtained that lore from Kavi.

95.s:
kacād bṛhaspatiś cāpi tato devāḥ pṛthak pṛthak
avāpur mahatīṃ vidyāṃ yām āhur mṛtajīvinīm //
95.d:
कचाद् बृहस्पतिश् चापि ततो देवाः पृथक् पृथक्
अवापुर् महतीं विद्यां याम् आहुर् मृतजीविनीम् ॥
95.m: From Kaca, Bṛhaspati as well, and then the gods one by one, / obtained the great lore which is called the reviver of the dead.

95.s:
yatra sā kavinā prāptā vidyāpūjya maheśvaram
gautamyā uttare pāre śukratīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
95.d:
यत्र सा कविना प्राप्ता विद्यापूज्य महेश्वरम्
गौतम्या उत्तरे पारे शुक्रतीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
95.m: Where that lore was obtained by Kavi having worshipped Maheśvara, / on the northern bank of the Gautamī, is called Śukratīrtha.

95.s:
mṛtasaṃjīvinītīrtham āyurārogyavardhanam
snānaṃ dānaṃ ca yat kiṃcit sarvam akṣayapuṇyadam //
95.d:
मृतसंजीविनीतीर्थम् आयुरारोग्यवर्धनम्
स्नानं दानं च यत् किंचित् सर्वम् अक्षयपुण्यदम् ॥
95.m: The Mṛtasaṃjīvinī tīrtha increases longevity and health; / whatever bathing and gift [is performed there], it all grants imperishable merit.

96.s:
brahmovāca
indratīrtham iti khyātaṃ brahmahatyāvināśanam
smaraṇād api pāpaughakleśasaṃghavināśanam //
96.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं ब्रह्महत्याविनाशनम्
स्मरणाद् अपि पापौघक्लेशसंघविनाशनम् ॥
96.m: Brahmā said: / Known as Indratīrtha, it destroys [the sin of] killing a brahmin; / even by memory of it, the mass of sins and multitude of afflictions are destroyed.

96.s:
purā vṛtravadhe vṛtte brahmahatyā tu nārada
śacīpatiṃ cānugatā tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītavad dhariḥ //
96.d:
पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते ब्रह्महत्या तु नारद
शचीपतिं चानुगता तां दृष्ट्वा भीतवद् धरिः ॥
96.m: Formerly, when the slaying of Vṛtra took place, [the sin of] killing a brahmin, O Nārada, / pursued Śacī's husband; seeing it, Hari, as if terrified—

96.s:
indras tato vṛtrahantā itaś cetaś ca dhāvati
yatra yatra tv asau yāti hatyā sāpīndragāminī //
96.d:
इन्द्रस् ततो वृत्रहन्ता इतश् चेतश् च धावति
यत्र यत्र त्व् असौ याति हत्या सापीन्द्रगामिनी ॥
96.m: Then Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, ran hither and thither; / wherever he went, that [brahman-]murder also followed Indra.

96.s:
sa mahat sara āviśya padmanālam upāgamat
tatrāsau tantuvad bhūtvā vāsaṃ cakre śacīpatiḥ //
96.d:
स महत् सर आविश्य पद्मनालम् उपागमत्
तत्रासौ तन्तुवद् भूत्वा वासं चक्रे शचीपतिः ॥
96.m: Entering a great lake, he crept into a lotus stalk; / there, becoming fine as a thread, Śacī's lord took up his abode.

96.s:
sarastīre 'pi hatyāsīd divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam
etasminn antare devā nirindrā hy abhavan mune //
96.d:
सरस्तीरे ऽपि हत्यासीद् दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम्
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे देवा निरिन्द्रा ह्य् अभवन् मुने ॥
96.m: And on the bank of the lake, the murder waited for a divine thousand years. / In the meantime, O sage, the gods became indraless.

96.s:
mantrayām āsur avyagrāḥ katham indro bhaved iti
tatrāham avadaṃ devān hatyāsthānaṃ prakalpya ca //
96.d:
मन्त्रयाम् आसुर् अव्यग्राः कथम् इन्द्रो भवेद् इति
तत्राहम् अवदं देवान् हत्यास्थानं प्रकल्प्य च ॥
96.m: Undismayed, they deliberated: "How can there be an Indra?" / There I spoke to the gods, having assigned a place for the murder:

96.s:
indrasya pāvanārthāya gautamyām abhiṣicyatām
yatrābhiṣiktaḥ pūtātmā punar indro bhaviṣyati //
96.d:
इन्द्रस्य पावनार्थाय गौतम्याम् अभिषिच्यताम्
यत्राभिषिक्तः पूतात्मा पुनर् इन्द्रो भविष्यति ॥
96.m: "For the purification of Indra, let him be consecrated in the Gautamī; / where, having been consecrated, his self purified, he will again become Indra."

96.s:
tathā te niścayaṃ kṛtvā gautamīṃ śīghram āgaman
tatra snātaṃ surapatiṃ devāś ca ṛṣayas tathā //
96.d:
तथा ते निश्चयं कृत्वा गौतमीं शीघ्रम् आगमन्
तत्र स्नातं सुरपतिं देवाश् च ऋषयस् तथा ॥
96.m: Having thus made their resolve, they swiftly went to the Gautamī; / there, when the lord of the gods had bathed, the gods and sages likewise,

96.s:
abhiṣektukāmās te sarve śacīkāntaṃ ca tasthire
abhiṣicyamānam indraṃ taṃ prakopād gautamo 'bravīt //
96.d:
अभिषेक्तुकामास् ते सर्वे शचीकान्तं च तस्थिरे
अभिषिच्यमानम् इन्द्रं तं प्रकोपाद् गौतमो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
96.m: all wishing to consecrate Śacī's beloved, took their stand. / As Indra was being consecrated, Gautama said in great fury:

96.s:
gautama uvāca
abhiṣekṣyanti pāpiṣṭhaṃ mahendraṃ gurutalpagam
tān sarvān bhasmasāt kuryāṃ śīghraṃ yāntv asurārayaḥ //
96.d:
गौतम उवाच
अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति पापिष्ठं महेन्द्रं गुरुतल्पगम्
तान् सर्वान् भस्मसात् कुर्यां शीघ्रं यान्त्व् असुरारयः ॥
96.m: Gautama said: / "If they consecrate the wicked Mahendra, who defiled his guru's bed, / I will reduce them all to ashes! Let the enemies of the asuras depart swiftly!"

96.s:
brahmovāca
tad ṛṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā parihṛtya ca gautamīm
narmadām agaman sarva indram ādāya satvarāḥ //
96.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् ऋषेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा परिहृत्य च गौतमीम्
नर्मदाम् अगमन् सर्व इन्द्रम् आदाय सत्वराः ॥
96.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of the sage and leaving the Gautamī, / they all quickly took Indra and went to the Narmadā.

96.s:
uttare narmadātīre abhiṣekāya tasthire
abhiṣekṣyamāṇam indraṃ taṃ māṇḍavyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ //
96.d:
उत्तरे नर्मदातीरे अभिषेकाय तस्थिरे
अभिषेक्ष्यमाणम् इन्द्रं तं माण्डव्यो भगवान् ऋषिः ॥
96.m: On the northern bank of the Narmadā they stood ready for the consecration. / As Indra was about to be consecrated, the venerable sage Māṇḍavya

96.s:
abravīd bhasmasāt kuryāṃ yadi syād abhiṣecanam
pūjayām āsur amarā māṇḍavyaṃ yuktibhiḥ stavaiḥ //
96.d:
अब्रवीद् भस्मसात् कुर्यां यदि स्याद् अभिषेचनम्
पूजयाम् आसुर् अमरा माण्डव्यं युक्तिभिः स्तवैः ॥
96.m: said: "I will reduce [you] to ashes if the consecration takes place!" / The immortals worshipped Māṇḍavya with reasoned arguments and hymns of praise.

96.s:
devā ūcuḥ
ayam indraḥ sahasrākṣo yasmin deśe 'bhiṣicyate
tatrātidāruṇaṃ vighnaṃ mune samupajāyate //
96.d:
देवा ऊचुः
अयम् इन्द्रः सहस्राक्षो यस्मिन् देशे ऽभिषिच्यते
तत्रातिदारुणं विघ्नं मुने समुपजायते ॥
96.m: The gods said: / "In whatever place this thousand-eyed Indra is consecrated, / a very dreadful obstacle arises there, O sage.

96.s:
tacchāntiṃ kuru kalyāṇa prasīda varado bhava
malaniryātanaṃ yasmin kurmas tasmin varān bahūn //
96.d:
तच्छान्तिं कुरु कल्याण प्रसीद वरदो भव
मलनिर्यातनं यस्मिन् कुर्मस् तस्मिन् वरान् बहून् ॥
96.m: Bring about its appeasement, O auspicious one! Be pleased, be a giver of boons! / In whatever region we perform the removal of his taint,

96.s:
deśe dāsyāmahe sarve tad anujñātum arhasi
yasmin deśe surendrasya abhiṣeko bhaviṣyati //
96.d:
देशे दास्यामहे सर्वे तद् अनुज्ञातुम् अर्हसि
यस्मिन् देशे सुरेन्द्रस्य अभिषेको भविष्यति ॥
96.m: we shall all grant many boons to that region; you ought to permit it. / In the region where the consecration of the lord of the gods will take place,

96.s:
sa sarvakāmadaḥ puṃsāṃ dhānyavṛkṣaphalair yutaḥ
nānāvṛṣṭir na durbhikṣaṃ bhaved atra kadācana //
96.d:
स सर्वकामदः पुंसां धान्यवृक्षफलैर् युतः
नानावृष्टिर् न दुर्भिक्षं भवेद् अत्र कदाचन ॥
96.m: it shall grant all desires to men, endowed with grain, trees, and fruits; / here there shall never be untimely rain or famine."

96.s:
brahmovāca
mene tato muniśreṣṭho māṇḍavyo lokapūjitaḥ
abhiṣekaḥ kṛtas tatra malaniryātanaṃ tathā //
96.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मेने ततो मुनिश्रेष्ठो माण्डव्यो लोकपूजितः
अभिषेकः कृतस् तत्र मलनिर्यातनं तथा ॥
96.m: Brahmā said: / Then the best of sages, Māṇḍavya, revered by the world, assented; / the consecration was performed there, and likewise the removal of the taint.

96.s:
devais tadokto munibhiḥ sa deśo mālavas tataḥ
abhiṣikte surapatau jāte ca vimale tadā //
96.d:
देवैस् तदोक्तो मुनिभिः स देशो मालवस् ततः
अभिषिक्ते सुरपतौ जाते च विमले तदा ॥
96.m: Because it was addressed then by the gods [and] sages, that region was called Mālava thereafter. / When the lord of the gods was consecrated and had become free of taint,

96.s:
ānīya gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ taṃ puṇyāyābhiṣecire
surāś ca ṛṣayaś caiva ahaṃ viṣṇus tathaiva ca //
96.d:
आनीय गौतमीं गङ्गां तं पुण्यायाभिषेचिरे
सुराश् च ऋषयश् चैव अहं विष्णुस् तथैव च ॥
96.m: bringing the Gautamī Gaṅgā, the gods and sages, / and I and Viṣṇu likewise, consecrated him for [greater] sanctity;

96.s:
vasiṣṭho gautamaś cāpi agastyo 'triś ca kaśyapaḥ
ete cānye ca ṛṣayo devā yakṣāḥ sapannagāḥ //
96.d:
वसिष्ठो गौतमश् चापि अगस्त्यो ऽत्रिश् च कश्यपः
एते चान्ये च ऋषयो देवा यक्षाः सपन्नगाः ॥
96.m: Vasiṣṭha and Gautama, Agastya, Atri, and Kaśyapa, / these and other sages, gods, yakṣas, together with serpents,

96.s:
snānaṃ tatpuṇyatoyena akurvann abhiṣecanam
mayā punaḥ śacībhartā kamaṇḍalubhavena ca //
96.d:
स्नानं तत्पुण्यतोयेन अकुर्वन्न् अभिषेचनम्
मया पुनः शचीभर्ता कमण्डलुभवेन च ॥
96.m: performed his ablution and consecration with its sacred water. / Furthermore, Śacī's lord was consecrated by me with water arisen from my water-pot,

96.s:
vāriṇāpy abhiṣiktaś ca tatra puṇyābhavan nadī
siktā ceti ca tatrāsīt te gaṅgāyāṃ ca saṃgate //
96.d:
वारिणाप्य् अभिषिक्तश् च तत्र पुण्याभवन् नदी
सिक्ता चेति च तत्रासीत् ते गङ्गायां च संगते ॥
96.m: and there arose the holy river Puṇyā, / and there was the Siktā; both met at the Gaṅgā.

96.s:
saṃgamau tatra vikhyātau sarvadā munisevitau
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ puṇyāsaṃgamam ucyate //
96.d:
संगमौ तत्र विख्यातौ सर्वदा मुनिसेवितौ
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पुण्यासंगमम् उच्यते ॥
96.m: The two confluences there are renowned, always frequented by sages; / from that time forward that tīrtha is called Puṇyāsaṃgama.

96.s:
siktāyāḥ saṃgame puṇyam aindraṃ tad abhidhīyate
tatra sapta sahasrāṇi tīrthāny āsañ śubhāni ca //
96.d:
सिक्तायाः संगमे पुण्यम् ऐन्द्रं तद् अभिधीयते
तत्र सप्त सहस्राणि तीर्थान्य् आसञ् शुभानि च ॥
96.m: The confluence of the Siktā is called the holy Aindra tīrtha. / There seven thousand auspicious tīrthas came into being.

96.s:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa tu saṃgame
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ vidyān nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
96.d:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च विशेषेण तु संगमे
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं विद्यान् नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
96.m: Bathing and giving in them, especially at the confluence— / one should know all that to be imperishable; there should be no doubt about this.

96.s:
yad etat puṇyam ākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhec ca śṛṇoti vā
sarvapāpaiḥ sa mucyeta manovākkāyakarmajaiḥ //
96.d:
यद् एतत् पुण्यम् आख्यानं यः पठेच् च शृणोति वा
सर्वपापैः स मुच्येत मनोवाक्कायकर्मजैः ॥
96.m: Whoever recites or hears this sacred narrative / will be freed from all sins born of mind, speech, and bodily action.

97.s:
brahmovāca
paulastyaṃ tīrtham ākhyātaṃ sarvasiddhipradaṃ nṛṇām
prabhāvaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi bhraṣṭarājyapradāyakam //
97.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पौलस्त्यं तीर्थम् आख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं नृणाम्
प्रभावं तस्य वक्ष्यामि भ्रष्टराज्यप्रदायकम् ॥
97.m: Brahmā said: / The Paulastya tīrtha has been proclaimed, bestowing all accomplishments on men; / I will declare its power, which restores a lost kingdom.

97.s:
uttarāśāpatiḥ pūrvam ṛddhisiddhisamanvitaḥ
purā laṅkāpatiś cāsīj jyeṣṭho viśravasaḥ sutaḥ //
97.d:
उत्तराशापतिः पूर्वम् ऋद्धिसिद्धिसमन्वितः
पुरा लङ्कापतिश् चासीज् ज्येष्ठो विश्रवसः सुतः ॥
97.m: Formerly, the lord of the northern quarter, endowed with prosperity and perfection, / the eldest son of Viśravas, was the lord of Laṅkā.

97.s:
tasyaite bhrātaraś cāsan balavanto 'mitaprabhāḥ
sāpatnā rāvaṇaś caiva kumbhakarṇo vibhīṣaṇaḥ //
97.d:
तस्यैते भ्रातरश् चासन् बलवन्तो ऽमितप्रभाः
सापत्ना रावणश् चैव कुम्भकर्णो विभीषणः ॥
97.m: His half-brothers, mighty and of boundless splendour, / were Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vibhīṣaṇa.

97.s:
te 'pi viśravasaḥ putrā rākṣasyāṃ rākṣasās tu te
maddattena vimānena dhanado bhrātṛbhiḥ saha //
97.d:
ते ऽपि विश्रवसः पुत्रा राक्षस्यां राक्षसास् तु ते
मद्दत्तेन विमानेन धनदो भ्रातृभिः सह ॥
97.m: They too were sons of Viśravas, but born of a rākṣasī, and were rākṣasas. / By means of an aerial chariot given by me, Dhanada, along with his brothers,

97.s:
mamāntikaṃ bhaktiyukto nityam eti tu yāti ca
rāvaṇasya tu yā mātā kupitā sābravīt sutān //
97.d:
ममान्तिकं भक्तियुक्तो नित्यम् एति तु याति च
रावणस्य तु या माता कुपिता साब्रवीत् सुतान् ॥
97.m: used to come and go constantly into my presence, filled with devotion. / But Rāvaṇa's mother became enraged and spoke to her sons:

97.s:
rāvaṇamātovāca
mariṣye na ca jīviṣye putrā vairūpyakāraṇāt
devāś ca dānavāś cāsan sāpatnā bhrātaro mithaḥ //
97.d:
रावणमातोवाच
मरिष्ये न च जीविष्ये पुत्रा वैरूप्यकारणात्
देवाश् च दानवाश् चासन् सापत्ना भ्रातरो मिथः ॥
97.m: Rāvaṇa's mother said: / "I shall die, I will not live, O sons, on account of this humiliation! / The gods and the dānavas were half-brothers to one another;

97.s:
anyonyavadham īpsante jayaiśvaryavaśānugāḥ
tadbhavanto na puruṣā na śaktā na jayaiṣiṇaḥ
sāpatnyaṃ yo 'numanyate tasya jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
97.d:
अन्योन्यवधम् ईप्सन्ते जयैश्वर्यवशानुगाः
तद्भवन्तो न पुरुषा न शक्ता न जयैषिणः
सापत्न्यं यो ऽनुमन्यते तस्य जीवो निरर्थकः ॥
97.m: subject to the sway of victory and sovereignty, they seek each other's destruction. / Therefore you are not men, nor powerful, nor desirous of victory! / Whoever tolerates rivalry with a co-wife's son, his life is meaningless!"

97.s:
brahmovāca
tan mātṛvacanaṃ śrutvā bhrātaras te trayo mune
jagmus te tapase 'raṇyaṃ kṛtavantas tapo mahat //
97.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तन् मातृवचनं श्रुत्वा भ्रातरस् ते त्रयो मुने
जग्मुस् ते तपसे ऽरण्यं कृतवन्तस् तपो महत् ॥
97.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of their mother, those three brothers, O sage, / went to the forest for austerities and performed great asceticism.

97.s:
matto varān avāpuś ca traya ete ca rākṣasāḥ
mātulena marīcena tathā mātāmahena tu //
97.d:
मत्तो वरान् अवापुश् च त्रय एते च राक्षसाः
मातुलेन मरीचेन तथा मातामहेन तु ॥
97.m: And from me these three rākṣasas obtained boons. / At the instigation of their maternal uncle Marīca and also their maternal grandfather,

97.s:
tanmātṛvacanāc cāpi tato laṅkām ayācata
rakṣobhāvān mātṛdoṣād bhrātror vairam abhūn mahat //
97.d:
तन्मातृवचनाच् चापि ततो लङ्काम् अयाचत
रक्षोभावान् मातृदोषाद् भ्रात्रोर् वैरम् अभून् महत् ॥
97.m: and by their mother's word, [Rāvaṇa] then demanded Laṅkā. / Due to the rākṣasa nature and the mother's fault, great enmity arose between the two brothers.

97.s:
tatas tad abhavad yuddhaṃ devadānavayor iva
yuddhe jitvāgrajaṃ śāntaṃ dhanadaṃ bhrātaraṃ tathā //
97.d:
ततस् तद् अभवद् युद्धं देवदानवयोर् इव
युद्धे जित्वाग्रजं शान्तं धनदं भ्रातरं तथा ॥
97.m: Then a battle took place like that between the gods and dānavas; / having conquered in battle his peaceful elder brother Dhanada,

97.s:
puṣpakaṃ ca purīṃ laṅkāṃ sarvaṃ caiva vyapāharat
rāvaṇo ghoṣayām āsa trailokye sacarācare //
97.d:
पुष्पकं च पुरीं लङ्कां सर्वं चैव व्यपाहरत्
रावणो घोषयाम् आस त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे ॥
97.m: he seized the Puṣpaka, the city of Laṅkā, and everything else. / Rāvaṇa caused a proclamation to be made throughout the three worlds, with all that is moving and unmoving:

97.s:
yo dadyād āśrayaṃ bhrātuḥ sa ca vadhyo bhaven mama
bhrātrā nirasto vaiśravaṇo naiva prāpāśrayaṃ kvacit
pitāmahaṃ pulastyaṃ taṃ gatvā natvābravīd vacaḥ //
97.d:
यो दद्याद् आश्रयं भ्रातुः स च वध्यो भवेन् मम
भ्रात्रा निरस्तो वैश्रवणो नैव प्रापाश्रयं क्वचित्
पितामहं पुलस्त्यं तं गत्वा नत्वाब्रवीद् वचः ॥
97.m: "Whoever gives shelter to my brother, he shall be killed by me!" / Banished by his brother, Vaiśravaṇa found no shelter anywhere; / going to his grandfather Pulastya and bowing down, he spoke these words:

97.s:
dhanada uvāca
bhrātrā nirasto duṣṭena kiṃ karomi vadasva me
āśrayaḥ śaraṇaṃ yat syād daivaṃ vā tīrtham eva ca //
97.d:
धनद उवाच
भ्रात्रा निरस्तो दुष्टेन किं करोमि वदस्व मे
आश्रयः शरणं यत् स्याद् दैवं वा तीर्थम् एव च ॥
97.m: Dhanada said: / "Banished by my wicked brother, tell me, what should I do? / What shelter, refuge, deity, or tīrtha may there be?"

97.s:
brahmovāca
tat pautravacanaṃ śrutvā pulastyo vākyam abravīt //
97.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तत् पौत्रवचनं श्रुत्वा पुलस्त्यो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
97.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of his grandson, Pulastya spoke these words:

97.s:
pulastya uvāca
gautamīṃ gaccha putra tvaṃ stuhi devaṃ maheśvaram
tatra nāsya praveśaḥ syād gaṅgāyā jalamadhyataḥ //
97.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच
गौतमीं गच्छ पुत्र त्वं स्तुहि देवं महेश्वरम्
तत्र नास्य प्रवेशः स्याद् गङ्गाया जलमध्यतः ॥
97.m: Pulastya said: / "Go to the Gautamī, O son, and praise the god Maheśvara; / he cannot enter there, within the water of the Gaṅgā.

97.s: siddhiṃ prāpsyasi kalyāṇīṃ tathā kuru mayā saha //
97.d: सिद्धिं प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणीं तथा कुरु मया सह ॥
97.m: You will attain auspicious success; do so together with me."

97.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā jagāmāsau sabhāryo dhanadas tathā
pitrā mātrā ca vṛddhena pulastyena dhaneśvaraḥ //
97.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा जगामासौ सभार्यो धनदस् तथा
पित्रा मात्रा च वृद्धेन पुलस्त्येन धनेश्वरः ॥
97.m: Brahmā said: / Saying "So be it," Dhanada departed with his wife; / and together with his father, mother, and aged Pulastya, the lord of wealth went.

97.s:
gatvā tu gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ śuciḥ snātvā yatavrataḥ
tuṣṭāva devadeveśaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ śivam //
97.d:
गत्वा तु गौतमीं गङ्गां शुचिः स्नात्वा यतव्रतः
तुष्टाव देवदेवेशं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शिवम् ॥
97.m: Having gone to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, purified, having bathed and restrained his vows, / he praised Śiva, the lord of the gods, who bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation:

97.s:
dhanada uvāca
svāmī tvam evāsya carācarasya
viśvasya śaṃbho na paro 'sti kaścit
tvām apy avajñāya yadīha mohāt
pragalbhate kopi sa śocya eva
97.d:
धनद उवाच
स्वामी त्वम् एवास्य चराचरस्य
विश्वस्य शंभो न परो ऽस्ति कश्चित्
त्वाम् अप्य् अवज्ञाय यदीह मोहात्
प्रगल्भते कोपि स शोच्य एव
97.m: Dhanada said: / "You alone are the master of this universe, moving and unmoving, / O Śambhu; there is none other! / If anyone here, having disregarded even you, should behave insolently / out of delusion, he is truly to be pitied."

97.s:
tvam aṣṭamūrtyā sakalaṃ bibharṣi
tvadājñayā vartata eva sarvam
tathāpi vedeti budho bhavantaṃ
na jātv avidvān mahimā purātanam
97.d:
त्वम् अष्टमूर्त्या सकलं बिभर्षि
त्वदाज्ञया वर्तत एव सर्वम्
तथापि वेदेति बुधो भवन्तं
न जात्व् अविद्वान् महिमा पुरातनम्
97.m: You support everything through your eightfold form; / everything moves solely by your command. / Even so, the wise man knows you as such, / while the ignorant man never knows your primeval majesty.

97.s:
malaprasūtaṃ yad avocad ambā
hāsyāt suto 'yaṃ tava deva śūraḥ
tvatprekṣitād yaḥ sa ca vighnarājo
jajñe tv aho ceṣṭitam īśadṛṣṭeḥ
97.d:
मलप्रसूतं यद् अवोचद् अम्बा
हास्यात् सुतो ऽयं तव देव शूरः
त्वत्प्रेक्षिताद् यः स च विघ्नराजो
जज्ञे त्व् अहो चेष्टितम् ईशदृष्टेः
97.m: When the Mother said in jest of what was born from bodily impurity, / 'This heroic child is your son, O Lord,' / and that Lord of Obstacles was born from your gaze— / oh, how wondrous is the action of the Lord's glance!

97.s:
aśruplutāṅgī girijā samīkṣya
viyuktadāṃpatyam itīśam ūce
manobhavo 'bhūn madano ratiś ca
saubhāgyapūrvatvam avāpa somāt
97.d:
अश्रुप्लुताङ्गी गिरिजा समीक्ष्य
वियुक्तदांपत्यम् इतीशम् ऊचे
मनोभवो ऽभून् मदनो रतिश् च
सौभाग्यपूर्वत्वम् अवाप सोमात्
97.m: Seeing the mountain-born goddess her limbs bathed in tears, / the Lord said thus: 'Let the couple be reunited.' / Love, born of the mind, came to life, and Rati / attained her former good fortune from Soma.

97.s:
brahmovāca
ityādi stuvatas tasya purato 'bhūt trilocanaḥ
vareṇa cchandayām āsa harṣān novāca kiṃcana //
97.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्यादि स्तुवतस् तस्य पुरतो ऽभूत् त्रिलोचनः
वरेण च्छन्दयाम् आस हर्षान् नोवाच किंचन ॥
97.m: Brahmā said: / As he was praising him thus, the three-eyed Lord appeared before him / and offered him a boon; out of joy he said nothing at all.

97.s:
tūṣṇīṃbhūte tu dhanade pulastye ca maheśvare
punaḥ punar varasveti śive vādini harṣite //
97.d:
तूष्णींभूते तु धनदे पुलस्त्ये च महेश्वरे
पुनः पुनर् वरस्वेति शिवे वादिनि हर्षिते ॥
97.m: While Dhanada fell silent, and Pulastya and Maheśvara were there, / and Śiva, delighted, repeatedly said, 'Choose a boon!'—

97.s:
etasminn antare tatra vāg uvācāśarīriṇī
prāptavyaṃ dhanapālatvaṃ vadantīdaṃ maheśvaram //
97.d:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी
प्राप्तव्यं धनपालत्वं वदन्तीदं महेश्वरम् ॥
97.m: at that moment a bodiless voice spoke there, / saying this to Maheśvara: 'He must attain the guardianship of wealth.'

97.s:
pulastyasya tu yac cittaṃ pitur vaiśravaṇasya tu
viditveva tadā vāṇī śubham artham udīrayat //
97.d:
पुलस्त्यस्य तु यच् चित्तं पितुर् वैश्रवणस्य तु
विदित्वेव तदा वाणी शुभम् अर्थम् उदीरयत् ॥
97.m: As though knowing the mind of Pulastya / and of the father Vaiśravaṇa, the voice then uttered an auspicious purpose:

97.s:
bhūtavad bhavitavyaṃ syād dāsyamānaṃ tu dattavat
prāptavyaṃ prāptavat tatra daivī vāg abhavac chubhā //
97.d:
भूतवद् भवितव्यं स्याद् दास्यमानं तु दत्तवत्
प्राप्तव्यं प्राप्तवत् तत्र दैवी वाग् अभवच् छुभा ॥
97.m: 'Let what must be happen as though already done, and what is to be given as though already given; / let what is to be attained be as though attained.' There the divine voice was auspicious.

97.s:
prabhūtaśatruḥ paribhūtaduḥkhaḥ
saṃpūjya someśvaram āpa liṅgam
digīśvaratvaṃ draviṇaprabhutvam
apāradātṛtvakalatraputrān
97.d:
प्रभूतशत्रुः परिभूतदुःखः
संपूज्य सोमेश्वरम् आप लिङ्गम्
दिगीश्वरत्वं द्रविणप्रभुत्वम्
अपारदातृत्वकलत्रपुत्रान्
97.m: Having abundant enemies and overcoming his sorrow, / he worshipped the liṅga Someśvara and attained / lordship over the directions, mastery of wealth, / boundless generosity, wives, and sons.

97.s:
tāṃ vācaṃ dhanadaḥ śrutvā devadevaṃ triśūlinam
evaṃ bhavatu nāmeti dhanado vākyam abravīt //
97.d:
तां वाचं धनदः श्रुत्वा देवदेवं त्रिशूलिनम्
एवं भवतु नामेति धनदो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥
97.m: Hearing that voice, Dhanada addressed the God of Gods, / the trident-bearer, saying: 'So be it indeed.'

97.s:
tathaivāstv iti deveśo daivīṃ vācam amanyata
pulastyaṃ ca varaiḥ puṇyais tathā viśravasaṃ munim //
97.d:
तथैवास्त्व् इति देवेशो दैवीं वाचम् अमन्यत
पुलस्त्यं च वरैः पुण्यैस् तथा विश्रवसं मुनिम् ॥
97.m: The Lord of the Gods assented to the divine voice, saying, 'So let it be,' / and gratified Pulastya with holy boons, as well as the sage Viśravas.

97.s:
dhanapālaṃ ca deveśo hy abhinandya yayau śivaḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ paulastyaṃ dhanadaṃ viduḥ //
97.d:
धनपालं च देवेशो ह्य् अभिनन्द्य ययौ शिवः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पौलस्त्यं धनदं विदुः ॥
97.m: The Lord of the Gods, Śiva, commended Dhanapāla and departed. / From that time forth, they know that holy bathing place as Paulastya and Dhanada.

97.s:
tathā vaiśravasaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham
teṣu snānādi yat kiṃcit tat sarvaṃ bahupuṇyadam //
97.d:
तथा वैश्रवसं पुण्यं सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम्
तेषु स्नानादि यत् किंचित् तत् सर्वं बहुपुण्यदम् ॥
97.m: And likewise the holy Vaiśravasa, auspicious, granting all desires. / Whatever bathing and other rites are performed there, all that bestows great merit.

98.s:
brahmovāca
agnitīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvakratuphalapradam
sarvavighnopaśamanaṃ tattīrthasya phalaṃ śṛṇu //
98.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अग्नितीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम्
सर्वविघ्नोपशमनं तत्तीर्थस्य फलं शृणु ॥
98.m: Brahmā said: / Renowned as Agnitīrtha, it grants the fruit of all rituals / and pacifies all obstacles. Hear the fruit of that holy place:

98.s:
jātavedā iti khyāto agner bhrātā sa havyavāṭ
havyaṃ vahantaṃ devānāṃ gautamyās tīra eva tu //
98.d:
जातवेदा इति ख्यातो अग्नेर् भ्राता स हव्यवाट्
हव्यं वहन्तं देवानां गौतम्यास् तीर एव तु ॥
98.m: Known as Jātavedas, he was Agni's brother, the bearer of oblations. / As he was carrying the sacrificial offering of the gods on the very bank of the Gautamī,

98.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ sattrasadane agner bhrātaram uttamam
bhrātuḥ priyaṃ tathā dakṣaṃ madhur ditisuto balī //
98.d:
ऋषीणां सत्त्रसदने अग्नेर् भ्रातरम् उत्तमम्
भ्रातुः प्रियं तथा दक्षं मधुर् दितिसुतो बली ॥
98.m: in the sacrificial hall of the sages, that excellent brother of Agni, / dear to his brother and capable, the mighty Diti-son Madhu

98.s:
jaghāna ṛṣimukhyeṣu paśyatsu ca sureṣv api
havyaṃ devā naiva cāpur mṛte vai jātavedasi //
98.d:
जघान ऋषिमुख्येषु पश्यत्सु च सुरेष्व् अपि
हव्यं देवा नैव चापुर् मृते वै जातवेदसि ॥
98.m: slew, while the foremost sages and even the gods looked on. / And when Jātavedas was dead, the gods obtained no sacrificial food at all.

98.s:
mṛte bhrātari sa tv agniḥ priye vai jātavedasi
kopena mahatāviṣṭo gāṅgam ambhaḥ samāviśat //
98.d:
मृते भ्रातरि स त्व् अग्निः प्रिये वै जातवेदसि
कोपेन महताविष्टो गाङ्गम् अम्भः समाविशत् ॥
98.m: When his brother, his dear Jātavedas, was dead, / Agni, overcome with great rage, plunged into the waters of the Gaṅgā.

98.s:
gaṅgāmbhasi samāviṣṭe hy agnau devāś ca mānuṣāḥ
jīvam utsarjayām āsur agnijīvā yato matāḥ //
98.d:
गङ्गाम्भसि समाविष्टे ह्य् अग्नौ देवाश् च मानुषाः
जीवम् उत्सर्जयाम् आसुर् अग्निजीवा यतो मताः ॥
98.m: When Agni had entered the waters of the Gaṅgā, gods and humans / abandoned their life-breath, since they are considered to live by fire.

98.s:
yatrāgnir jalam āviṣṭas taṃ deśaṃ sarva eva te
ājagmur vibudhāḥ sarva ṛṣayaḥ pitaras tathā //
98.d:
यत्राग्निर् जलम् आविष्टस् तं देशं सर्व एव ते
आजग्मुर् विबुधाः सर्व ऋषयः पितरस् तथा ॥
98.m: Where Agni had entered the water, to that place all of them came— / all the deities, the sages, and the ancestors.

98.s:
vināgninā na jīvāmaḥ stuvanto 'gniṃ viśeṣataḥ
agniṃ jalagataṃ dṛṣṭvā priyaṃ cocur divaukasaḥ //
98.d:
विनाग्निना न जीवामः स्तुवन्तो ऽग्निं विशेषतः
अग्निं जलगतं दृष्ट्वा प्रियं चोचुर् दिवौकसः ॥
98.m: Saying, 'Without fire we do not live,' praising Agni exceedingly, / and seeing Agni residing in the water, the denizens of heaven spoke kindly to him.

98.s:
devā ūcuḥ
devāñ jīvaya havyena kavyena ca pitṝṃs tathā
mānuṣān annapākena bījānāṃ kledanena ca //
98.d:
देवा ऊचुः
देवाञ् जीवय हव्येन कव्येन च पितॄंस् तथा
मानुषान् अन्नपाकेन बीजानां क्लेदनेन च ॥
98.m: The gods said: / Revive the gods with the offering to the gods, and likewise the ancestors with the offering to the manes, / and humans by the cooking of food and the moistening of seeds.

98.s:
brahmovāca
agnir apy āha tān devāñ śakto yo me gato 'nujaḥ
kriyamāṇe bhavatkārye yā gatir jātavedasaḥ //
98.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अग्निर् अप्य् आह तान् देवाञ् शक्तो यो मे गतो ऽनुजः
क्रियमाणे भवत्कार्ये या गतिर् जातवेदसः ॥
98.m: Brahmā said: / Agni also said to those gods: 'My capable younger brother is gone; / the fate that befell Jātavedas while performing your task,

98.s:
sā vāpi syān mama surā notsahe kāryasādhane
kāryaṃ tu sarvatas tasya bhavatāṃ jātavedasaḥ //
98.d:
सा वापि स्यान् मम सुरा नोत्सहे कार्यसाधने
कार्यं तु सर्वतस् तस्य भवतां जातवेदसः ॥
98.m: that very fate may befall me too, O gods; I dare not accomplish the task. / Yet that task of yours was accomplished everywhere by Jātavedas.

98.s:
imāṃ sthitim anuprāpto na jāne me kathaṃ bhavet
iha cāmutra ca vyāptau śaktir apy atra no bhavet //
98.d:
इमां स्थितिम् अनुप्राप्तो न जाने मे कथं भवेत्
इह चामुत्र च व्याप्तौ शक्तिर् अप्य् अत्र नो भवेत् ॥
98.m: Having reached this state, I do not know how it will be for me; / nor would I have the power to pervade both here and the hereafter.'

98.s:
athāpi kriyamāṇe vai kārye saiva gatir mama
devās tam ūcur bhāvena sarveṇa ṛṣayas tathā //
98.d:
अथापि क्रियमाणे वै कार्ये सैव गतिर् मम
देवास् तम् ऊचुर् भावेन सर्वेण ऋषयस् तथा ॥
98.m: And yet, [he said,] 'If the task is performed, that same fate will be mine.' / The gods and the sages spoke to him with all affection:

98.s:
āyuḥ karmaṇi ca prītir vyāptau śaktiś ca dīyate
prayājān anuyājāṃś ca dāsyāmo havyavāhana //
98.d:
आयुः कर्मणि च प्रीतिर् व्याप्तौ शक्तिश् च दीयते
प्रयाजान् अनुयाजांश् च दास्यामो हव्यवाहन ॥
98.m: 'Longevity and pleasure in your work, and the power of pervasion are granted; / and we shall grant the fore-offerings and the after-offerings, O bearer of oblations!

98.s:
devānāṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ śreṣṭham āhutyaḥ prathamās tava
tvayā dattaṃ tu yad dravyaṃ bhokṣyāmaḥ surasattama //
98.d:
देवानां त्वं मुखं श्रेष्ठम् आहुत्यः प्रथमास् तव
त्वया दत्तं तु यद् द्रव्यं भोक्ष्यामः सुरसत्तम ॥
98.m: You are the supreme mouth of the gods; the first offerings are yours; / whatever substance is given by you, that we shall enjoy, O best of gods!'

98.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tuṣṭo 'bhavad vahnir devavākyād yathākramam
iha cāmutra ca vyāptau havye vā laukike tathā //
98.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तुष्टो ऽभवद् वह्निर् देववाक्याद् यथाक्रमम्
इह चामुत्र च व्याप्तौ हव्ये वा लौकिके तथा ॥
98.m: Brahmā said: / Then fire was satisfied in due course by the word of the gods, / to pervade both here and the hereafter, whether in the sacred offering or in worldly affairs.

98.s:
sarvatra vahnir abhayaḥ samartho 'bhūt surājñayā
jātavedā bṛhadbhānuḥ saptārcir nīlalohitaḥ //
98.d:
सर्वत्र वह्निर् अभयः समर्थो ऽभूत् सुराज्ञया
जातवेदा बृहद्भानुः सप्तार्चिर् नीललोहितः ॥
98.m: Fire became fearless and capable everywhere by the command of the gods— / Jātavedas, Bṛhadbhānu, seven-flamed, blue-and-red;

98.s:
jalagarbhaḥ śamīgarbho yajñagarbhaḥ sa ucyate
jalād ākṛṣya vibudhā abhiṣicya vibhāvasum //
98.d:
जलगर्भः शमीगर्भो यज्ञगर्भः स उच्यते
जलाद् आकृष्य विबुधा अभिषिच्य विभावसुम् ॥
98.m: he is called born of the water, born of the śamī tree, and born of the sacrifice. / Having drawn the fire out of the water and consecrated him,

98.s:
ubhayatra pade vāsaḥ sarvago 'gnis tato 'bhavat
yathāgataṃ surā jagmur vahnitīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
98.d:
उभयत्र पदे वासः सर्वगो ऽग्निस् ततो ऽभवत्
यथागतं सुरा जग्मुर् वह्नितीर्थं तद् उच्यते ॥
98.m: fire then became all-pervading, dwelling in both realms. / The gods went away as they had come; that is called Vahnitīrtha.

98.s:
tatra sapta śatāny āsaṃs tīrthāni guṇavanti ca
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yaḥ karoti jitātmavān //
98.d:
तत्र सप्त शतान्य् आसंस् तीर्थानि गुणवन्ति च
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च यः करोति जितात्मवान् ॥
98.m: There were seven hundred virtuous holy places there; / whoever performs bathing and giving in them, self-controlled,

98.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ sāgraṃ prāpnoty avikalaṃ śubham
devatīrthaṃ ca tatraiva āgneyaṃ jātavedasam //
98.d:
अश्वमेधफलं साग्रं प्राप्नोत्य् अविकलं शुभम्
देवतीर्थं च तत्रैव आग्नेयं जातवेदसम् ॥
98.m: obtains the complete, entire, auspicious fruit of a horse-sacrifice. / Right there is the Devatīrtha, related to Agni and Jātavedas.

98.s:
agnipratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃ tatrāste 'nekavarṇavat
taddevadarśanād eva sarvakratuphalaṃ labhet //
98.d:
अग्निप्रतिष्ठितं लिङ्गं तत्रास्ते ऽनेकवर्णवत्
तद्देवदर्शनाद् एव सर्वक्रतुफलं लभेत् ॥
98.m: A liṅga established by Agni stands there, having various colors; / merely by seeing that deity, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.

99.s:
brahmovāca
ṛṇapramocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ vedavido viduḥ
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tanmanāḥ //
99.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ऋणप्रमोचनं नाम तीर्थं वेदविदो विदुः
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तन्मनाः ॥
99.m: Brahmā said: / Those who know the Vedas know of a holy place named Ṛṇapramocana; / I shall explain its nature—listen with attentive mind, O Nārada!

99.s:
āsīt pṛthuśravā nāma priyaḥ kakṣīvataḥ sutaḥ
na dārasaṃgrahaṃ lebhe vairāgyān nāgnipūjanam //
99.d:
आसीत् पृथुश्रवा नाम प्रियः कक्षीवतः सुतः
न दारसंग्रहं लेभे वैराग्यान् नाग्निपूजनम् ॥
99.m: There was a dear son of Kakṣīvat named Pṛthuśravas; / because of dispassion, he did not take a wife nor did he worship the sacred fires.

99.s:
kanīyāṃs tu samartho 'pi parivittibhayān mune
nākarod dārakarmādi naivāgnīnām upāsanam //
99.d:
कनीयांस् तु समर्थो ऽपि परिवित्तिभयान् मुने
नाकरोद् दारकर्मादि नैवाग्नीनाम् उपासनम् ॥
99.m: The younger brother, though capable, out of fear of marrying before his elder brother, O sage, / did not perform the marriage rites and so forth, nor did he attend to the fires.

99.s:
tataḥ procuḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ putraṃ kakṣīvataḥ śubham
jyeṣṭhaṃ caiva kaniṣṭhaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthag idaṃ vacaḥ //
99.d:
ततः प्रोचुः पितृगणाः पुत्रं कक्षीवतः शुभम्
ज्येष्ठं चैव कनिष्ठं च पृथक् पृथग् इदं वचः ॥
99.m: Then the hosts of ancestors addressed the auspicious sons of Kakṣīvat, / the elder and the younger, each with these words:
The ancestors said: / 'To dispel the three debts, let marriage be undertaken!'

99.s:
brahmovāca
nety uvāca tato jyeṣṭhaḥ kim ṛṇaṃ kena yujyate
kanīyāṃs tu pitṝn prāha na yogyo dārasaṃgrahaḥ //
99.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उवाच ततो ज्येष्ठः किम् ऋणं केन युज्यते
कनीयांस् तु पितॄन् प्राह न योग्यो दारसंग्रहः ॥
99.m: Brahmā said: / Then the elder said, 'No! What debt is bound to whom?' / But the younger said to the ancestors, 'Marriage is not proper for me

99.s:
jyeṣṭhe sati mahāprājñaḥ parivittibhayād iti
tāv ubhau punar apy evam ūcus te vai pitāmahāḥ //
99.d:
ज्येष्ठे सति महाप्राज्ञः परिवित्तिभयाद् इति
ताव् उभौ पुनर् अप्य् एवम् ऊचुस् ते वै पितामहाः ॥
99.m: while the elder is here, out of fear of marrying before the elder,' O very wise one. / To both of them those grandfathers spoke again thus:

99.s:
pitara ūcuḥ
yātām ubhau gautamīṃ tu puṇyāṃ kakṣīvataḥ sutau
kurutāṃ gautamīsnānaṃ sarvābhīṣṭapradāyakam //
99.d:
पितर ऊचुः
याताम् उभौ गौतमीं तु पुण्यां कक्षीवतः सुतौ
कुरुतां गौतमीस्नानं सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायकम् ॥
99.m: The ancestors said: / 'Let both sons of Kakṣīvat go to the holy Gautamī; / perform the Gautamī bath, which grants all desired things.'

99.s:
gacchatāṃ gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ lokatritayapāvanīm
snānaṃ ca tarpaṇaṃ tasyāṃ kurutāṃ śraddhayānvitau //
99.d:
गच्छतां गौतमीं गङ्गां लोकत्रितयपावनीम्
स्नानं च तर्पणं तस्यां कुरुतां श्रद्धयान्वितौ ॥
99.m: “Let them go to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds, / and let both perform bathing and water-offerings in it, endowed with faith.

99.s:
dṛṣṭāvanāmitā dhyātā gautamī sarvakāmadā
na deśakālajātyādiniyamo 'trāvagāhane
jyeṣṭho 'nṛṇas tato bhūyāt parivittir na cetaraḥ //
99.d:
दृष्टावनामिता ध्याता गौतमी सर्वकामदा
न देशकालजात्यादिनियमो ऽत्रावगाहने
ज्येष्ठो ऽनृणस् ततो भूयात् परिवित्तिर् न चेतरः ॥
99.m: When seen, bowed to, and meditated upon, the Gautamī fulfills all desires. / There is no restriction of place, time, caste, or anything else for plunging into it here. / Then the elder brother will be free of debt, and the other will not become a younger brother married before the elder.”

99.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ pṛthuśravā jyeṣṭhaḥ kṛtvā snānaṃ satarpaṇam
trayāṇām api lokānāṃ kākṣīvato 'nṛṇo 'bhavat //
99.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः पृथुश्रवा ज्येष्ठः कृत्वा स्नानं सतर्पणम्
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानां काक्षीवतो ऽनृणो ऽभवत् ॥
99.m: Brahmā said: / Then Pṛthuśravas, the elder, having performed the bath together with water-offerings, / Kakṣīvat’s son, became free of debt to the three worlds as well.

99.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham ṛṇamocanam ucyate
śrautasmārta-ṛṇebhyaś ca itarebhyaś ca nārada
tatra snānena dānena ṛṇī muktaḥ sukhī bhavet //
99.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् ऋणमोचनम् उच्यते
श्रौतस्मार्त-ऋणेभ्यश् च इतरेभ्यश् च नारद
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन ऋणी मुक्तः सुखी भवेत् ॥
99.m: From then on, that sacred place is called Ṛṇamocana. / From debts prescribed by Vedic and traditional authority, and from others, O Nārada, / by bathing and giving gifts there, a debtor will become free and happy.

100.s:
brahmovāca
suparṇāsaṃgamaṃ nāma kādravāsaṃgamaṃ tathā
maheśvaro yatra devo gaṅgāpulinam āśritaḥ //
100.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सुपर्णासंगमं नाम काद्रवासंगमं तथा
महेश्वरो यत्र देवो गङ्गापुलिनम् आश्रितः ॥
100.m: Brahmā said: / There is the confluence called Suparṇāsaṃgama, and likewise the Kādravāsaṃgama, / where the god Maheśvara resides on the sandy bank of the Gaṅgā.

100.s:
agnikuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva raudraṃ vaiṣṇavam eva ca
sauraṃ saumyaṃ tathā brāhmaṃ kaumāraṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā //
100.d:
अग्निकुण्डं च तत्रैव रौद्रं वैष्णवम् एव च
सौरं सौम्यं तथा ब्राह्मं कौमारं वारुणं तथा ॥
100.m: And right there is the Agnikuṇḍa, and the pool belonging to Rudra, that to Viṣṇu, / that to Sūrya, that to Soma, likewise to Brahmā, to Kumāra, and likewise to Varuṇa;

100.s:
apsarā ca nadī yatra saṃgatā gaṅgayā tathā
tattīrthasmaraṇād eva kṛtakṛtyo bhaven naraḥ //
100.d:
अप्सरा च नदी यत्र संगता गङ्गया तथा
तत्तीर्थस्मरणाद् एव कृतकृत्यो भवेन् नरः ॥
100.m: and where the Apsaras River also joins with the Gaṅgā. / Merely from remembering that sacred place, a man will have accomplished his purpose.

100.s:
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ śṛṇu yatnena nārada
indreṇa hiṃsitāḥ pūrvaṃ vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ
dattārdhatapasaḥ sarve procus te kāśyapaṃ munim //
100.d:
सर्वपापप्रशमनं शृणु यत्नेन नारद
इन्द्रेण हिंसिताः पूर्वं वालखिल्या महर्षयः
दत्तार्धतपसः सर्वे प्रोचुस् ते काश्यपं मुनिम् ॥
100.m: Listen attentively, O Nārada, to that which quells all sins. / Formerly, the great sages, the Vālakhilyas, were harmed by Indra. / Having offered half their ascetic fervor, they all spoke to the sage Kaśyapa.

100.s:
vālakhilyā ūcuḥ
putram utpādayānena indradarpaharaṃ śubham
tapaso 'rdhaṃ tu dāsyāmas tathety āha munis tu tān //
100.d:
वालखिल्या ऊचुः
पुत्रम् उत्पादयानेन इन्द्रदर्पहरं शुभम्
तपसो ऽर्धं तु दास्यामस् तथेत्य् आह मुनिस् तु तान् ॥
100.m: The Vālakhilyas said: / “By means of this, beget an auspicious son who will destroy Indra’s pride. / We shall give half our ascetic fervor.” The sage said to them: “So be it.”

100.s:
suparṇāyāṃ tato garbham ādadhe sa prajāpatiḥ
kadrvāṃ caiva śanair brahman sarpāṇāṃ sarpamātari //
100.d:
सुपर्णायां ततो गर्भम् आदधे स प्रजापतिः
कद्र्वां चैव शनैर् ब्रह्मन् सर्पाणां सर्पमातरि ॥
100.m: Then that lord of creatures placed an embryo in Suparṇā, / and also, O brahman, slowly in Kadrū, the mother of serpents.

100.s:
te garbhiṇyāv ubhe āha gantukāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ
aparādho na ca kvāpi kāryo gamanam eva ca //
100.d:
ते गर्भिण्याव् उभे आह गन्तुकामः प्रजापतिः
अपराधो न च क्वापि कार्यो गमनम् एव च ॥
100.m: Desiring to depart, the lord of creatures said to both pregnant wives: / “No transgression must be committed anywhere, nor should you wander away.

100.s: anyatra gamanāc chāpo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
100.d: अन्यत्र गमनाच् छापो भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
100.m: From going elsewhere, a curse will follow without doubt.”

100.s:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā sa yayau patnyau gate bhartari te ubhe
tadaiva jagmatuḥ sattram ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām //
100.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा स ययौ पत्न्यौ गते भर्तरि ते उभे
तदैव जग्मतुः सत्त्रम् ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम् ॥
100.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, he went away. When their husband had departed, those two wives / went right then to a sacrificial session of the sages of purified self,

100.s:
brahmavṛndasamākīrṇaṃ gaṅgātīrasamāśritam
unmatte te ubhe nityaṃ vayaḥsaṃpattigarvite //
100.d:
ब्रह्मवृन्दसमाकीर्णं गङ्गातीरसमाश्रितम्
उन्मत्ते ते उभे नित्यं वयःसंपत्तिगर्विते ॥
100.m: which was crowded with an assembly of Brahmā’s offspring, situated on the bank of the Gaṅgā. / Those two were continually reckless, proud of their youth and prosperity.

100.s:
nivāryamāṇe bahuśo munibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ
vikurvatyau tatra sattre samāni ca havīṃṣi ca //
100.d:
निवार्यमाणे बहुशो मुनिभिस् तत्त्वदर्शिभिः
विकुर्वत्यौ तत्र सत्त्रे समानि च हवींषि च ॥
100.m: Though restrained many times by the sages who saw reality, / they disrupted the sacrificial offerings and sacrificial materials in that sacrificial session.

100.s:
yoṣitāṃ durvilasitaṃ kaḥ saṃvaritum īśvaraḥ
te dṛṣṭvā cukṣubhur viprā apamārgarate ubhe //
100.d:
योषितां दुर्विलसितं कः संवरितुम् ईश्वरः
ते दृष्ट्वा चुक्षुभुर् विप्रा अपमार्गरते उभे ॥
100.m: Who is able to hold back the wicked wantonness of women? / Seeing the two devoted to wrongful ways, the brahmins were agitated:

100.s:
apamārgasthite yasmād āpage hi bhaviṣyathaḥ
suparṇā caiva kadrūś ca nadyau te saṃbabhūvatuḥ //
100.d:
अपमार्गस्थिते यस्माद् आपगे हि भविष्यथः
सुपर्णा चैव कद्रूश् च नद्यौ ते संबभूवतुः ॥
100.m: “Because you stand on a wrongful path, you will become rivers!” / And so Suparṇā and Kadrū became two rivers.

100.s:
sa kadācid gṛhaṃ prāyāt kaśyapo 'tha prajāpatiḥ
ṛṣibhyas tatra vṛttāntaṃ śāpaṃ tābhyāṃ savistaram //
100.d:
स कदाचिद् गृहं प्रायात् कश्यपो ऽथ प्रजापतिः
ऋषिभ्यस् तत्र वृत्तान्तं शापं ताभ्यां सविस्तरम् ॥
100.m: Then, at some time, Kaśyapa, the lord of creatures, came home. / Having heard from the sages the full account of the curse upon them,

100.s:
śrutvā tu vismayāviṣṭaḥ kiṃ karomīty acintayat
ṛṣibhyaḥ kathayām āsa vālakhilyā iti śrutāḥ //
100.d:
श्रुत्वा तु विस्मयाविष्टः किं करोमीत्य् अचिन्तयत्
ऋषिभ्यः कथयाम् आस वालखिल्या इति श्रुताः ॥
100.m: overcome with astonishment, he thought: “What shall I do?” / He spoke to the sages who are known as the Vālakhilyas.

100.s:
ta ūcuḥ kaśyapaṃ vipraṃ gatvā gaṅgāṃ tu gautamīm
tatra stuhi maheśānaṃ punar bhārye bhaviṣyataḥ //
100.d:
त ऊचुः कश्यपं विप्रं गत्वा गङ्गां तु गौतमीम्
तत्र स्तुहि महेशानं पुनर् भार्ये भविष्यतः ॥
100.m: They said to the brahmin Kaśyapa: “Having gone to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, / praise Maheśāna there; they will become wives again.

100.s:
brahmahatyābhayād eva yatra devo maheśvaraḥ
gaṅgāmadhye sadā hy āste madhyameśvarasaṃjñayā //
100.d:
ब्रह्महत्याभयाद् एव यत्र देवो महेश्वरः
गङ्गामध्ये सदा ह्य् आस्ते मध्यमेश्वरसंज्ञया ॥
100.m: Where, solely out of fear of killing a brahmin, the god Maheśvara / always resides in the midst of the Gaṅgā under the name Madhyameśvara.”

100.s:
tathety uktvā kaśyapo 'pi snātvā gaṅgāṃ jitavrataḥ
tuṣṭāva stavanaiḥ puṇyair devadevaṃ maheśvaram //
100.d:
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा कश्यपो ऽपि स्नात्वा गङ्गां जितव्रतः
तुष्टाव स्तवनैः पुण्यैर् देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ॥
100.m: Saying “So be it,” Kaśyapa also bathed in the Gaṅgā, firm in his vow, / and praised the god of gods, Maheśvara, with holy hymns of praise.

100.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
lokatrayaikādhipater na yasya
kutrāpi vastuny abhimānaleśaḥ
sa siddhanātho 'khilaviśvakartā
bhartā śivāyā bhavatu prasannaḥ
100.d:
कश्यप उवाच
लोकत्रयैकाधिपतेर् न यस्य
कुत्रापि वस्तुन्य् अभिमानलेशः
स सिद्धनाथो ऽखिलविश्वकर्ता
भर्ता शिवाया भवतु प्रसन्नः
100.m: Kaśyapa said: / “May the husband of Śivā be gracious—the sole sovereign of the three worlds, / who has not the slightest trace of pride toward any object whatsoever, / the lord of perfected beings, the creator of the entire universe.

100.s:
tāpatrayoṣṇadyutitāpitānām
itas tato vai paridhāvatāṃ ca
śarīriṇāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ
tvam eva duḥkhavyapanodadakṣaḥ
100.d:
तापत्रयोष्णद्युतितापितानाम्
इतस् ततो वै परिधावतां च
शरीरिणां स्थावरजङ्गमानां
त्वम् एव दुःखव्यपनोददक्षः
100.m: For embodied beings, both stationary and moving, / who are scorched by the blazing heat of the three afflictions and who run here and there, / you alone are skilled in removing sorrow.

100.s:
sattvādiyogas trividho 'pi yasya
śakrādibhir vaktum aśakya eva
vicitravṛttiṃ paricintya somaṃ
sukhī sadā dānaparo vareṇyaḥ
100.d:
सत्त्वादियोगस् त्रिविधो ऽपि यस्य
शक्रादिभिर् वक्तुम् अशक्य एव
विचित्रवृत्तिं परिचिन्त्य सोमं
सुखी सदा दानपरो वरेण्यः
100.m: Whose threefold connection with sattva and the other gunas / is impossible to describe even by Indra and the gods; / contemplating him who has wondrous activities, who is accompanied by Umā, / one is always happy, devoted to generosity, the most excellent.”

100.s:
brahmovāca
ityādistutibhir devaḥ stuto gaurīpatiḥ śivaḥ
prasanno hy adadāc chaṃbhuḥ kaśyapāya varān bahūn //
100.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्यादिस्तुतिभिर् देवः स्तुतो गौरीपतिः शिवः
प्रसन्नो ह्य् अददाच् छंभुः कश्यपाय वरान् बहून् ॥
100.m: Brahmā said: / Having been praised with these and other hymns, the god Śiva, Gaurī’s husband, / Śambhu, pleased, granted many boons to Kaśyapa.

100.s:
bhāryārthinaṃ tu taṃ prāha syātāṃ bhārye ubhe tu te
nadīsvarūpe patnyau ye gaṅgāṃ prāpya saridvarām //
100.d:
भार्यार्थिनं तु तं प्राह स्यातां भार्ये उभे तु ते
नदीस्वरूपे पत्न्यौ ये गङ्गां प्राप्य सरिद्वराम् ॥
100.m: To him who sought his wives, he said: “Let those two be your wives. / The two wives who have the nature of rivers, upon reaching the Gaṅgā, best of streams,

100.s:
tatsaṃgamanamātreṇa tābhyāṃ bhūyāt svakaṃ vapuḥ
te garbhiṇyau punar jāte gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ //
100.d:
तत्संगमनमात्रेण ताभ्यां भूयात् स्वकं वपुः
ते गर्भिण्यौ पुनर् जाते गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः ॥
100.m: merely by confluence with it, will regain their own forms.” / And by the favor of the Gaṅgā, they became pregnant once again.

100.s:
tataḥ prajāpatiḥ prīto bhārye prāpya mahāmanāḥ
āhvayām āsa tān viprān gautamītīram āśritān //
100.d:
ततः प्रजापतिः प्रीतो भार्ये प्राप्य महामनाः
आह्वयाम् आस तान् विप्रान् गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितान् ॥
100.m: Then the lord of creatures, large-minded, pleased at regaining his two wives, / invited the brahmins residing on the bank of the Gautamī.

100.s:
sīmantonnayanaṃ cakre tābhyāṃ prītaḥ prajāpatiḥ
brāhmaṇān pūjayām āsa vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā //
100.d:
सीमन्तोन्नयनं चक्रे ताभ्यां प्रीतः प्रजापतिः
ब्राह्मणान् पूजयाम् आस विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
100.m: The lord of creatures, delighted, performed the hair-parting rite for them, / and honored the brahmins with the rites prescribed by rule.

100.s:
bhuktavatsv atha vipreṣu kaśyapasyātha mandire
bhartṛsamīpopaviṣṭā kadrūr viprān nirīkṣya ca //
100.d:
भुक्तवत्स्व् अथ विप्रेषु कश्यपस्याथ मन्दिरे
भर्तृसमीपोपविष्टा कद्रूर् विप्रान् निरीक्ष्य च ॥
100.m: Then, when the brahmins had eaten in the house of Kaśyapa, / Kadrū, seated beside her husband, looked at the brahmins.

100.s:
tataḥ kadrūr ṛṣīn akṣṇā prāhasat te ca cukṣubhuḥ
yenākṣṇā hasitā pāpe bhajyatāṃ te 'kṣi pāpavat //
100.d:
ततः कद्रूर् ऋषीन् अक्ष्णा प्राहसत् ते च चुक्षुभुः
येनाक्ष्णा हसिता पापे भज्यतां ते ऽक्षि पापवत् ॥
100.m: Then Kadrū laughed at the sages with her eye, and they were agitated: / “O sinful woman, the eye with which you laughed shall be destroyed, like a sinful woman!”

100.s:
kāṇābhavat tataḥ kadrūḥ sarpamāteti yocyate
tataḥ prasādayām āsa kaśyapo bhagavān ṛṣīn //
100.d:
काणाभवत् ततः कद्रूः सर्पमातेति योच्यते
ततः प्रसादयाम् आस कश्यपो भगवान् ऋषीन् ॥
100.m: Then Kadrū, who is called the mother of serpents, became one-eyed. / Then the venerable Kaśyapa propitiated the sages.

100.s:
tataḥ prasannās te procur gautamī saritāṃ varā
aparādhasahasrebhyo rakṣiṣyati ca sevanāt //
100.d:
ततः प्रसन्नास् ते प्रोचुर् गौतमी सरितां वरा
अपराधसहस्रेभ्यो रक्षिष्यति च सेवनात् ॥
100.m: Then, pleased, they said: “The Gautamī, the best of rivers, / will protect her from thousands of offenses through attendance upon it.”

100.s:
bhāryānvitas tathā cakre kaśyapo munisattamaḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham ubhayoḥ saṃgamaṃ viduḥ
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvakratuphalapradam //
100.d:
भार्यान्वितस् तथा चक्रे कश्यपो मुनिसत्तमः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् उभयोः संगमं विदुः
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम् ॥
100.m: Together with his wife, Kaśyapa, best of sages, did so. / From then on, they know that sacred place as the confluence of the two, / which quells all sins and grants the fruit of all sacrifices.

101.s:
brahmovāca
purūravasam ākhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ vedavido viduḥ
smaraṇād eva pāpānāṃ nāśanaṃ kiṃ tu darśanāt //
101.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुरूरवसम् आख्यातं तीर्थं वेदविदो विदुः
स्मरणाद् एव पापानां नाशनं किं तु दर्शनात् ॥
101.m: Brahmā said: / Those who know the Veda know the sacred place called Purūravas; / it destroys sins merely by remembering it, how much more by beholding it!

101.s:
purūravā brahmasadaḥ prāpya tatra sarasvatīm
yadṛcchayā devanadīṃ hasantīṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpasaṃpannām urvaśīṃ prāha bhūpatiḥ //
101.d:
पुरूरवा ब्रह्मसदः प्राप्य तत्र सरस्वतीम्
यदृच्छया देवनदीं हसन्तीं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके
तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नाम् उर्वशीं प्राह भूपतिः ॥
101.m: Purūravas, having arrived at Brahmā’s assembly, saw there the Sarasvatī, / the river of the gods, who was laughing by chance near Brahmā; / seeing her endowed with beauty, the king said to Urvaśī:

101.s:
rājovāca
keyaṃ rūpavatī sādhvī sthiteyaṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike
sarvāsām uttamā yoṣid dīpayantī sabhām imām //
101.d:
राजोवाच
केयं रूपवती साध्वी स्थितेयं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके
सर्वासाम् उत्तमा योषिद् दीपयन्ती सभाम् इमाम् ॥
101.m: The king said: / “Who is this beautiful, virtuous woman standing near Brahmā, / the most excellent woman among all, illuminating this assembly?”

101.s:
brahmovāca
urvaśī prāha rājānam iyaṃ devanadī śubhā
sarasvatī brahmasutā nityam eti ca yāti ca
tac chrutvā vismito rājā ānayemāṃ mamāntikam //
101.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
उर्वशी प्राह राजानम् इयं देवनदी शुभा
सरस्वती ब्रह्मसुता नित्यम् एति च याति च
तच् छ्रुत्वा विस्मितो राजा आनयेमां ममान्तिकम् ॥
101.m: Brahmā said: / Urvaśī said to the king: “This is the auspicious celestial river, / the Sarasvatī, Brahmā’s daughter; she comes and goes constantly.” / Hearing that, the astonished king said: “Bring her to me.”

101.s:
brahmovāca
urvaśī punar apy āha rājānaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam //
101.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
उर्वशी पुनर् अप्य् आह राजानं भूरिदक्षिणम् ॥
101.m: Brahmā said: / Urvaśī spoke again to the king of generous sacrificial gifts:

101.s:
urvaśy uvāca
ānīyate mahārāja tasyāḥ sarvaṃ nivedya ca //
101.d:
उर्वश्य् उवाच
आनीयते महाराज तस्याः सर्वं निवेद्य च ॥
101.m: Urvaśī said: / “She will be brought, great king, after having informed her of everything.”

101.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tāṃ prāhiṇot tatra rājā prītyā tadorvaśīm
sā gatvā rājavacanaṃ nyavedayad athorvaśī //
101.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तां प्राहिणोत् तत्र राजा प्रीत्या तदोर्वशीम्
सा गत्वा राजवचनं न्यवेदयद् अथोर्वशी ॥
101.m: Brahmā said: / Then the king affectionately sent Urvaśī there. / Urvaśī, having gone, conveyed the king’s words.

101.s:
sarasvaty api tan mene urvaśyā yan niveditam
sā tatheti pratijñāya prāyād yatra purūravāḥ //
101.d:
सरस्वत्य् अपि तन् मेने उर्वश्या यन् निवेदितम्
सा तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय प्रायाद् यत्र पुरूरवाः ॥
101.m: The Sarasvatī agreed to what had been conveyed by Urvaśī. / Promising “So be it,” she went to where Purūravas was.

101.s:
sarasvatyās tatas tīre sa reme bahulāḥ samāḥ
sarasvān abhavat putro yasya putro bṛhadrathaḥ //
101.d:
सरस्वत्यास् ततस् तीरे स रेमे बहुलाः समाः
सरस्वान् अभवत् पुत्रो यस्य पुत्रो बृहद्रथः ॥
101.m: Then he took his pleasure on the bank of the Sarasvatī for many years. / Sarasvān became his son, whose son was Bṛhadratha.

101.s:
tāṃ gacchantīṃ nṛpagṛhaṃ nityam eva sarasvatīm
sarasvantaṃ tato lakṣma jñātvānyeṣu tathā kṛtam //
101.d:
तां गच्छन्तीं नृपगृहं नित्यम् एव सरस्वतीम्
सरस्वन्तं ततो लक्ष्म ज्ञात्वान्येषु तथा कृतम् ॥
101.m: To that Sarasvatī who was constantly going to the king's palace, / perceiving the mark of the ocean, it was done likewise to the others.

101.s:
tasyai dadāv ahaṃ śāpaṃ bhūyā iti mahānadī
macchāpabhītā vāgīśā prāgād devīṃ ca gautamīm //
101.d:
तस्यै ददाव् अहं शापं भूया इति महानदी
मच्छापभीता वागीशा प्रागाद् देवीं च गौतमीम् ॥
101.m: 'May you become a great river!'—I gave her this curse. / Frightened by my curse, the goddess of speech went to the divine Gautamī,

101.s:
kamaṇḍalubhavāṃ pūtāṃ mātaraṃ lokapāvanīm
tāpatrayopaśamanīm aihikāmuṣmikapradām //
101.d:
कमण्डलुभवां पूतां मातरं लोकपावनीम्
तापत्रयोपशमनीम् ऐहिकामुष्मिकप्रदाम् ॥
101.m: who was born from a water jar, pure, mother and purifier of the world, / pacifier of the threefold suffering, granter of this world and the next.

101.s:
sā gatvā gautamīṃ devīṃ prāha macchāpam āditaḥ
gaṅgāpi mām uvācedaṃ viśāpāṃ kartum arhasi //
101.d:
सा गत्वा गौतमीं देवीं प्राह मच्छापम् आदितः
गङ्गापि माम् उवाचेदं विशापां कर्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
101.m: She went to the goddess Gautamī and told her of my curse from the beginning. / Gaṅgā too spoke this to me: “You ought to free her from the curse.

101.s:
na yuktaṃ yat sarasvatyāḥ śāpaṃ tvaṃ dattavān asi
strīṇām eṣa svabhāvo vai puṃskāmā yoṣito yataḥ //
101.d:
न युक्तं यत् सरस्वत्याः शापं त्वं दत्तवान् असि
स्त्रीणाम् एष स्वभावो वै पुंस्कामा योषितो यतः ॥
101.m: It was not right that you cursed Sarasvatī. / Indeed, this is the nature of women, since women desire men.

101.s:
svabhāvacapalā brahman yoṣitaḥ sakalā api
tvaṃ kathaṃ tu na jānīṣe jagatsraṣṭāmbujāsana //
101.d:
स्वभावचपला ब्रह्मन् योषितः सकला अपि
त्वं कथं तु न जानीषे जगत्स्रष्टाम्बुजासन ॥
101.m: All women, O Brahmā, are fickle by nature. / How is it that you, the lotus-seated creator of the world, do not know this?

101.s:
viḍambayati kaṃ vā na kāmo vāpi svabhāvataḥ
tato viśāpam avadaṃ dṛśyāpi syāt sarasvatī //
101.d:
विडम्बयति कं वा न कामो वापि स्वभावतः
ततो विशापम् अवदं दृश्यापि स्यात् सरस्वती ॥
101.m: Whom does desire not mock by its very nature?” / Thereupon I spoke the release from the curse: “Sarasvatī shall also become visible.”

101.s:
tasmāc chāpān nadī martye dṛśyādṛśyā sarasvatī
yatraiṣā saṃgatā devī gaṅgāyāṃ śāpavihvalā //
101.d:
तस्माच् छापान् नदी मर्त्ये दृश्यादृश्या सरस्वती
यत्रैषा संगता देवी गङ्गायां शापविह्वला ॥
101.m: Because of that curse, Sarasvatī is both visible and invisible among mortals as a river. / Where this goddess, distraught by the curse, united with Gaṅgā,

101.s:
tatra prāyān nṛpavaro dhārmikaḥ sa purūravāḥ
tapas taptvā samārādhya devaṃ siddheśvaraṃ haram //
101.d:
तत्र प्रायान् नृपवरो धार्मिकः स पुरूरवाः
तपस् तप्त्वा समाराध्य देवं सिद्धेश्वरं हरम् ॥
101.m: there went that righteous Purūravas, best of kings. / Having performed austerities and propitiated the god Hara, the Lord of the Siddhas,

101.s:
sarvān kāmān athāvāpa gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ purūravasam ucyate //
101.d:
सर्वान् कामान् अथावाप गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पुरूरवसम् उच्यते ॥
101.m: he then attained all his desires through the grace of Gaṅgā. / From that time on, that tīrtha is called Paurūravasa.

101.s:
sarasvatīsaṃgamaṃ ca brahmatīrthaṃ tad ucyate
siddheśvaro yatra devaḥ sarvakāmapradaṃ tu tat //
101.d:
सरस्वतीसंगमं च ब्रह्मतीर्थं तद् उच्यते
सिद्धेश्वरो यत्र देवः सर्वकामप्रदं तु तत् ॥
101.m: It is also called the confluence of Sarasvatī and the tīrtha of Brahmā. / Where the god Siddheśvara resides, that [place] grants every desire.

102.s:
brahmovāca
sāvitrī caiva gāyatrī śraddhā medhā sarasvatī
etāni pañca tīrthāni puṇyāni munayo viduḥ //
102.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सावित्री चैव गायत्री श्रद्धा मेधा सरस्वती
एतानि पञ्च तीर्थानि पुण्यानि मुनयो विदुः ॥
